chapters.title: Chapter 5006: The Scale II
paragraphs: His voice dropped to something approaching solemnity.

"It is impossible. The door simply does not open for those who lack the key, and the key is not found among the Four Aspects no matter how thoroughly one masters them. Chaos may grant tremendous power within its domain. Paradox may permit contradictions that reshape local reality. Existence may build Civilizations spanning Primordial Realms. The First Tongue may rewrite the very language through which reality expresses itself."
He shook his head slowly, crystallized features shifting with the motion.

"But none of these authorities, magnificent as they may be, can carry a being past THE Second Scale. For that journey, one requires something deeper. Something that predates the Aspects themselves. Something that was present during THE First Cause and remains present still, flowing beneath the surface of what beings perceive as power."
Yggvaros paused in his contemplation and released a sigh carrying weight accumulated since before most Primordial Architects had achieved their first moments of cognizance.

He looked outward, his gaze piercing the white barrier emanating from the tree behind him. Beyond that calm boundary, the storms of corrupted paradoxical proto-matter continued their violent transformation of THE Prima Indifferentia. Blue-gold light pulsed through the chaos, Infinite Absolute Seals scattered across regions that had never known such authority before this current age.

"Infinity is unfathomably difficult to seek at THE Second Scale. Even those who have walked these heights for eons struggle to access more than fragments of its true nature. We sense it. We know it exists. We understand, in principle, what it represents. But channeling it? Directing it? Making it serve our purposes rather than simply existing in proximity to our awareness?"
His eyes narrowed with something approaching genuine interest.

"That requires methodology that most at this Scale have never developed. That requires understanding that most at this Scale have never achieved. That requires either tremendous fortune or tremendous insight, and fortune of such magnitude does not simply occur without cause."
His gaze focused more intently on the blue-gold light pulsing through the storms beyond his barrier.

"And yet someone astounding enough in Our Observable Existence has not only grasped Infinity, but they have spread it openly and freely for all others to see. The corruption carries it. The proto-matter pulses with it. Every corner of THE Prima Indifferentia now holds fragments of Infinite authority that did not exist here before this current transformation began."
Yggvaros raised one hand, his crystallized fingers moving with deliberate purpose.

"Is this merely their own Infinity, personal authority spread thin across vast distances? Or are they pulling from Infinity on the same level as THE Primordial Source, accessing depths that even those at THE Second Scale have found difficult to perceive? The distinction matters greatly, for the implications of each possibility diverge toward futures that could reshape everything we understand about advancement itself."

He waved his hand in sweeping motion, and the corruption beyond his barrier responded to his authority. The paradoxical proto-matter was filtered away, pushed aside by will refined across cycles beyond counting. What remained was pure, distilled from the chaos that had carried it.
Blue-gold Infinite Absolute Seals flowed into his domain, drawn through the white barrier by invitation rather than force.

Many across Observable Existence had already mixed their weavings with this paradoxical corrupted proto-matter and Infinity, their existences accelerating through combination that would either elevate them or unmake them depending on factors they likely did not understand.
Yggvaros had been careful not to touch it himself, maintaining the contemplative distance that had served him well since he first grasped THE Second Scale.
But at this time, curiosity overcame caution.
HUUM!

The weavings of Infinity fell into his hands, and a heartshaking aura erupted from his position with force pressing against regions of THE Prima Indifferentia far beyond his normal influence. The calm boundary around the white tree flickered as power flowed through crystallized fingers that had not touched authority this potent in eons.

Many Undivided Ones and Formless Terrors paused in their distant conflicts in different directions, sensing something that exceeded their comprehension emanating from a direction they instinctively knew to avoid.
Yggvaros pulled his hands back from the particles of Infinity.

"Utilizing Infinity greatly empowers and strengthens one’s Civilization, this much is certain. The authority flows through foundations and expands them, fills gaps that other methodologies cannot reach, elevates potential toward heights that seemed impossible before contact was established."
His voice carried weight now, informed by direct experience rather than mere contemplation.

"But those who channel it also add their power to Infinity itself. The exchange flows in both directions, and I wonder whether those currently mixing their weavings with this scattered authority understand what they contribute to something they cannot perceive. They take, yes, but they also give. And what they give flows toward a source that none here fully comprehend."
He looked down at the diagram he had drawn on the golden earth, at the branching lines leading from the Four Aspects toward that distant singularity labeled Scale of Existence.

"None here truly understand how to access THE Primordial Source. Perhaps those who naturally reach THE Second Scale might perceive pathways that others cannot. Perhaps eons of patient observation might reveal truths that desperate advancement obscures. Perhaps existence is simply too vast and unfathomable for any single consciousness to grasp, regardless of how long that consciousness has existed."
His gaze lifted toward the blue-gold light still pulsing beyond his barrier, toward the Infinity scattered across THE Prima Indifferentia by someone operating from Observable Existence.

"But what I am most curious about is the one who freely spread this authority. The foremost Guider of Infinity, or would they be called THE Conduit of Infinity? The terminology matters less than the reality of what they have accomplished."

Yggvaros rose from his seated position, his crystallized form shifting with motion that pressed against the golden earth beneath him. The white tree pulsed behind him as if acknowledging his contemplation, its dimensions continuing to vary with each moment that passed.

"How did you access Infinity when even those at THE Second Scale have found such access difficult? What methodology do you possess that we lack? What understanding have you achieved that has eluded beings who have existed since before THE Infinite Unfurling itself?"
His questions hung in the calm air of his domain, unanswered by anything except the distant storms continuing their transformation of THE Prima Indifferentia.
Somewhere in Observable Existence, a finite being conducted an endless sea.
And THE Arboreal Warden Yggvaros, First Among THE Sane to Grasp THE Second Scale of Existence, found himself genuinely curious about him!

He thought for a moment before he took out a small white notebook made from the same material as the tree at the center of this place. And in his hands, a white pen burning with authority appeared as he thought for a moment before opening the book that had half its pages filled, and he...began to write.
On the matter of Civilizations and their foundations, a lot of confusion persists among those who have not walked beyond THE First Scale of Existence.

It is common for such beings to observe authorities like Infinity and conclude that anything so vast must surely serve as the basis for a Way, for a Civilization, for the fundamental expression of one’s advancement through the hierarchies of power.
This confusion is understandable, for how could something so immense be anything other than what one builds upon?
Those at THE Second Scale know better.

Infinity is not a Civilization. It cannot be made into a Way. One may access it, channel it, allow it to flow through one’s foundations and empower what already exists there. But Infinity itself resists being claimed as personal territory in the manner that true Civilizations demand.
It is the river, not the vessel. It is the wind, not the sail. To confuse the force with the structure is to fundamentally misunderstand the nature of advancement itself.
The Four Aspects of the Oldest Paradox of Existence provide the true foundations from which Civilizations emerge.

From Chaos can spring the Civilization of Infernal Chaos, where destruction and creation dance in eternal cycles that feed upon themselves. From that same Aspect emerges the Civilization of Consuming Chaos, where all things are devoured to fuel further devouring, and the Civilization of Creative Chaos, where disorder births novelty without end.
The variations are as numerous as those who walk these paths, for Chaos by its nature refuses singular expression.

From Existence, the branches multiply further still. The Civilization of Unbound Existence permits one to transcend the limitations that constrain lesser beings, while the Civilization of Bound Existence finds power in accepting those limitations and forging strength from restriction.

The Civilization of Living Existence and its counterpart, the Civilization of Dead Existence, represent the fundamental duality that all things which are must eventually navigate. Higher variations include the Civilization of Transcendent Existence, where the boundaries between states of being dissolve entirely, and the Civilization of Primordial Existence, where one’s foundations touch the very origins from which all differentiation emerged.
Derivatives of wonders, you could even call them.
Paradox offers paths equally varied. The Civilization of Limitless Paradox permits contradictions to exist without resolution, drawing power from the tension between incompatible truths.

The Civilization of Dual Paradox maintains precisely two contradictory states in permanent opposition, while the Civilization of Recursive Paradox folds contradictions within contradictions until the very concept of resolution loses meaning.
Some speak of the Civilization of Resolved Paradox, though there is dispute whether true resolution remains paradoxical at all.

The First Tongue branches into linguistic expressions too numerous to fully catalog. The Civilization of Qi channels the fundamental energy underlying all speech and expression, while the Civilization of Logos builds foundations upon the rational structures through which reality organizes itself.

The Civilization of Phonemic Authority focuses on the individual sounds that compose meaning, and the Civilization of Lexical Dominion concerns itself with the accumulated weight of words combined into greater wholes.

Some pursue the Civilization of Silent Tongue, finding power in what is not spoken, while others walk the Civilization of Primal Utterance, seeking the first sounds ever differentiated from potential into expression.

All of these Civilizations exist. All of them can be walked by beings who achieved THE Second Scale and beyond. All of them draw from the Four Aspects in configurations as unique as the beings who claim them as of course, you do have those who purely claim Chaos, Paradox, Existence, and The First Tongue...well, not really The First Tongue as that is a hard one.
But you will never find one at THE Second Scale who speaks of the Civilization of Infinity.
For Infinity empowers Civilizations. It does not become them. Or so it is believed. On this, there really should not be an exception.

Those who attempt to make Infinity their Way find themselves conducting force without foundation, channeling authority without structure, wielding power that flows through them rather than from them. The distinction is subtle but absolute.

One may ride the river, but one cannot become the river while remaining oneself. One may harness the wind, but one cannot be the wind while retaining the identity necessary to harness anything at all.
This truth is rarely discussed among those at THE First Scale, for they have not yet perceived the difference between empowerment and foundation.

They see Infinity scattered across Observable Existence and conclude that someone must have built a Civilization upon it. They observe its effects and assume those effects represent advancement along familiar paths. Their confusion is forgivable, for they see only the surface of depths they cannot yet fathom.
And one should not even begin discussing THE Primordial Source.

Where Infinity is misunderstood, THE Primordial Source is simply unknown. Where Infinity can at least be perceived and channeled and directed toward purposes, THE Primordial Source resists even acknowledgment of its nature.
Those at THE Second Scale sense it as one senses a presence in a darkened room, knowing something exists without being able to identify what that something might be.
And unlike Infinity, which flows freely for those capable of conducting it, THE Primordial Source has never been accessed in Observable Existence as far as we can confirm.

Perhaps it cannot be channeled. Perhaps it can only be touched, briefly, by those who stumble upon it through fortune rather than methodology. Perhaps it is not a force at all but rather the absence from which all forces emerged, and attempting to channel absence is a contradiction even Paradox cannot resolve.
These questions remain unanswered.
They may remain unanswered forever.
—Excerpted from "Musings on Scales and Foundations," attributed to THE Arboreal Warden Yggvaros, date of composition unknown.

sentences.text: His voice dropped to something approaching solemnity.
"It is impossible.
The door simply does not open for those who lack the key, and the key is not found among the Four Aspects no matter how thoroughly one masters them.
Chaos may grant tremendous power within its domain.
Paradox may permit contradictions that reshape local reality.
Existence may build Civilizations spanning Primordial Realms.
The First Tongue may rewrite the very language through which reality expresses itself."
He shook his head slowly, crystallized features shifting with the motion.
"But none of these authorities, magnificent as they may be, can carry a being past THE Second Scale.
For that journey, one requires something deeper.
Something that predates the Aspects themselves.
Something that was present during THE First Cause and remains present still, flowing beneath the surface of what beings perceive as power."
Yggvaros paused in his contemplation and released a sigh carrying weight accumulated since before most Primordial Architects had achieved their first moments of cognizance.
He looked outward, his gaze piercing the white barrier emanating from the tree behind him.
Beyond that calm boundary, the storms of corrupted paradoxical proto-matter continued their violent transformation of THE Prima Indifferentia.
Blue-gold light pulsed through the chaos, Infinite Absolute Seals scattered across regions that had never known such authority before this current age.
"Infinity is unfathomably difficult to seek at THE Second Scale.
Even those who have walked these heights for eons struggle to access more than fragments of its true nature.
We sense it.
We know it exists.
We understand, in principle, what it represents.
But channeling it?
Directing it?
Making it serve our purposes rather than simply existing in proximity to our awareness?"
His eyes narrowed with something approaching genuine interest.
"That requires methodology that most at this Scale have never developed.
That requires understanding that most at this Scale have never achieved.
That requires either tremendous fortune or tremendous insight, and fortune of such magnitude does not simply occur without cause."
His gaze focused more intently on the blue-gold light pulsing through the storms beyond his barrier.
"And yet someone astounding enough in Our Observable Existence has not only grasped Infinity, but they have spread it openly and freely for all others to see.
The corruption carries it.
The proto-matter pulses with it.
Every corner of THE Prima Indifferentia now holds fragments of Infinite authority that did not exist here before this current transformation began."
Yggvaros raised one hand, his crystallized fingers moving with deliberate purpose.
"Is this merely their own Infinity, personal authority spread thin across vast distances?
Or are they pulling from Infinity on the same level as THE Primordial Source, accessing depths that even those at THE Second Scale have found difficult to perceive?
The distinction matters greatly, for the implications of each possibility diverge toward futures that could reshape everything we understand about advancement itself."
He waved his hand in sweeping motion, and the corruption beyond his barrier responded to his authority.
The paradoxical proto-matter was filtered away, pushed aside by will refined across cycles beyond counting.
What remained was pure, distilled from the chaos that had carried it.
Blue-gold Infinite Absolute Seals flowed into his domain, drawn through the white barrier by invitation rather than force.

Many across Observable Existence had already mixed their weavings with this paradoxical corrupted proto-matter and Infinity, their existences accelerating through combination that would either elevate them or unmake them depending on factors they likely did not understand.
Yggvaros had been careful not to touch it himself, maintaining the contemplative distance that had served him well since he first grasped THE Second Scale.
But at this time, curiosity overcame caution.
HUUM!
The weavings of Infinity fell into his hands, and a heartshaking aura erupted from his position with force pressing against regions of THE Prima Indifferentia far beyond his normal influence.
The calm boundary around the white tree flickered as power flowed through crystallized fingers that had not touched authority this potent in eons.

Many Undivided Ones and Formless Terrors paused in their distant conflicts in different directions, sensing something that exceeded their comprehension emanating from a direction they instinctively knew to avoid.
Yggvaros pulled his hands back from the particles of Infinity.
"Utilizing Infinity greatly empowers and strengthens one’s Civilization, this much is certain.
The authority flows through foundations and expands them, fills gaps that other methodologies cannot reach, elevates potential toward heights that seemed impossible before contact was established."
His voice carried weight now, informed by direct experience rather than mere contemplation.
"But those who channel it also add their power to Infinity itself.
The exchange flows in both directions, and I wonder whether those currently mixing their weavings with this scattered authority understand what they contribute to something they cannot perceive.
They take, yes, but they also give.
And what they give flows toward a source that none here fully comprehend."
He looked down at the diagram he had drawn on the golden earth, at the branching lines leading from the Four Aspects toward that distant singularity labeled Scale of Existence.
"None here truly understand how to access THE Primordial Source.
Perhaps those who naturally reach THE Second Scale might perceive pathways that others cannot.
Perhaps eons of patient observation might reveal truths that desperate advancement obscures.
Perhaps existence is simply too vast and unfathomable for any single consciousness to grasp, regardless of how long that consciousness has existed."
His gaze lifted toward the blue-gold light still pulsing beyond his barrier, toward the Infinity scattered across THE Prima Indifferentia by someone operating from Observable Existence.
"But what I am most curious about is the one who freely spread this authority.
The foremost Guider of Infinity, or would they be called THE Conduit of Infinity?
The terminology matters less than the reality of what they have accomplished."
Yggvaros rose from his seated position, his crystallized form shifting with motion that pressed against the golden earth beneath him.
The white tree pulsed behind him as if acknowledging his contemplation, its dimensions continuing to vary with each moment that passed.
"How did you access Infinity when even those at THE Second Scale have found such access difficult?
What methodology do you possess that we lack?
What understanding have you achieved that has eluded beings who have existed since before THE Infinite Unfurling itself?"
His questions hung in the calm air of his domain, unanswered by anything except the distant storms continuing their transformation of THE Prima Indifferentia.
Somewhere in Observable Existence, a finite being conducted an endless sea.
And THE Arboreal Warden Yggvaros, First Among THE Sane to Grasp THE Second Scale of Existence, found himself genuinely curious about him!
He thought for a moment before he took out a small white notebook made from the same material as the tree at the center of this place.
And in his hands, a white pen burning with authority appeared as he thought for a moment before opening the book that had half its pages filled, and he...began to write.
On the matter of Civilizations and their foundations, a lot of confusion persists among those who have not walked beyond THE First Scale of Existence.

It is common for such beings to observe authorities like Infinity and conclude that anything so vast must surely serve as the basis for a Way, for a Civilization, for the fundamental expression of one’s advancement through the hierarchies of power.
This confusion is understandable, for how could something so immense be anything other than what one builds upon?
Those at THE Second Scale know better.
Infinity is not a Civilization.
It cannot be made into a Way.
One may access it, channel it, allow it to flow through one’s foundations and empower what already exists there.
But Infinity itself resists being claimed as personal territory in the manner that true Civilizations demand.
It is the river, not the vessel.
It is the wind, not the sail.
To confuse the force with the structure is to fundamentally misunderstand the nature of advancement itself.

From Chaos can spring the Civilization of Infernal Chaos, where destruction and creation dance in eternal cycles that feed upon themselves.

chapters.title: Chapter 5007: Do Not Idolize I
paragraphs: In the outer fringes of Alfheimr.
Space fluctuated with distortions pressing against the boundaries of this Primordial Realm, reality bending and folding as something approached from directions that normal perception could not track.
The fluctuations intensified for a moment, building toward a crescendo of spatial displacement, and then three unique figures appeared where nothing had existed moments before.
Fresh arrivals from THE Interstices!

The first was an Undivided One in humanoid form, his skin shining obsidian with depths suggesting countless eyes watching from beneath that dark surface. He stood tall and proud, adorned in a clear blue robe that contrasted sharply with his darkness, and his features held an expressiveness unusual for beings of his classification.
Where most Undivided Ones presented faces of hunger and alien intent, this one smiled with genuine enthusiasm, his radiant eyes filled with expectations.
The second was a Formless Terror whose entire body consisted of illusory crimson tentacles, but they had been arranged and compressed into a humanoid shape held together with discipline.
Both were unique among their kinds, geniuses of their own stature whose power would have put common Absolutes to shame.
Floating behind them was a woman also adorned in blue robes, but the air surrounding her carried weight of an entirely different magnitude.

She held the aura of a Primordial Architect, that intersection of differentiation and undifferentiation pressing against reality with authority accumulated since THE First Cause itself. Her presence alone made the outer fringes of Alfheimr seem to contract slightly.

Her eyes were pure white, holding no iris or pupil in any conventional sense, but within that whiteness floated blue dots resembling singularities, points of compressed authority orbiting slowly through her gaze.
Radiant white hair cascaded down her back in waves holding their own faint luminescence. She was strikingly beautiful, and really, ridiculously so!
A Primordial Architect, an Undivided One, and a Formless Terror walked into Alfheimr.

This was not the start of a bad joke but an actual reality, three beings of vastly different classifications traveling together with purpose that had brought them across Observable Existence in search of something specific.
The blue robes they shared marked them as affiliated, as belonging to something greater than their individual natures.
The Formless Terror turned toward the Primordial Architect.
"Naldine, what do your senses tell you?"
His voice emerged from somewhere within that mass of illusory appendages.
"Is the Infinity-bearer in this Primordial Realm? We have been searching to no avail for a while now, and I confess my patience grows thin despite my best efforts to maintain it."
The Primordial Architect, Naldine, looked ahead with gaze piercing through layers of reality that her companions could not perceive.

The outer fringes of Alfheimr stretched before them in configurations of light and energy unique to this realm, forests of crystallized potential rising toward skies holding colors that had not fully differentiated into specific hues. Traces of authority lingered everywhere, remnants of beings who had passed through this space across eons of accumulated history.
And among those traces, faint but unmistakable, glimmers of Infinity pulsed with blue-gold light.
But they were old. Residual. The echoes of presence rather than presence itself.
Naldine shook her head with a motion carrying finality.
"He should not be here. He was here, but no more."
Her voice emerged cold and precise.
"Otherwise the pull of Infinity here would be much greater than what I perceive. What remains is merely what he left behind, traces of passage rather than indication of current location."
As she spoke, she raised one hand before her with deliberate slowness. On her palm, glimmers of Infinite Absolute Seals shimmered brightly.
She had been collecting these fragments throughout their journey, gathering pieces of the Infinity-bearer’s scattered influence like a hunter gathering tracks left by prey they had not yet glimpsed.
The eyes of the Undivided One, Arthur, shone brilliantly. His obsidian features shifted with expression holding something approaching reverence.

"The adversity that breaks all others shall forge him. The hardship that ends all paths shall begin his. The Scales demand what the Scales demand, and he shall pay in currencies that have not yet been minted."
His words emerged with cadence of recitation.

"Three times shall he face the mirror of undoing. Three times shall he choose between becoming and unbecoming. Three times shall the answer be the same, and three times shall the answer be different."
The crystallized trees seemed to lean away from his voice, as if even the environment of Alfheimr recognized the significance of what he spoke.
"In the end, which is also the beginning, the Infinite shall stand before the Undefined. And only one shall remain to tell the tale that no one shall hear."
Arthur paused, his obsidian features shifting into a smile holding genuine amusement.
"This is an Echo of First Cause."
The words he had uttered were heavy! But Arthur laughed after speaking them, the sound emerging bright and vibrant from his humanoid form.
"Haha! Do you think the Undefined that will stand before the Infinite is me? The Great Arthur!"
He spread his arms wide, blue robes billowing with the motion despite the absence of wind.

"We have been musing about this Echo since we first heard it, and I still do not know what much of it means. But I am more and more curious about the Infinity-bearer with each passing moment. If he can just show me how he utilizes Infinity and makes it do all the things he is making it do, all the wonders he accomplishes that we can only observe from afar..."
His eyes actually held a fervent light. He revered Infinity far too much, and that reverence colored everything he said about the one currently conducting it across Observable Existence.
Naldine’s gaze turned toward him with coldness pressing against his enthusiasm like ice against flame.
"Do not idolize him too much."
Her voice cut through his fervor with precision.

"In the grand scheme of existence, I consider him a fool due to his actions. Why spread Infinity across Observable Existence just because he has it? What purpose does such generosity serve when the recipients of that generosity become competitors for resources that should remain concentrated?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5008: Do Not Idolize II
paragraphs: The blue singularities in her white eyes orbited faster, conveying something approaching contempt.

"Sometimes great power can land on those who do not know how to use it. First, I have to meet him. If he is worthy, we will see what arrangements might be made. Until then, you two better not be embarrassments who grovel at his feet just because of Echoes of Causes you heard whispered across the void."
She stepped forward, her presence pressing against both Arthur and Gunther with weight reminding them exactly who led their particular association.

"We ultimately seek Infinity, not just the one who Guides it, however grand they may be. They are not synonymous with Infinity itself, just those capable of doing much more with it than the rest of us. The authority matters. The wielder is merely a obstacle or opportunity depending on how they respond to our approach."
Her cold gaze swept across both of them, demanding acknowledgment of her position.
"Okay? Arthur, Gunther, are you..."

She trailed off, her attention snapping toward the distance with sharpness that made both her companions turn to follow her gaze. The blue singularities in her eyes contracted to points of intense focus, and her beautiful features hardened into expression holding neither welcome nor hostility, only assessment.
In the distance, outlines were approaching through the crystallized forests of Alfheimr’s outer fringes.

An Absolute led the group, his form unmistakable. Two faces occupied a single head, one serene and one severe, both currently arranged into expressions of polite interest. He floated forward with casual grace, his authority pressing against the environment without demanding submission from it.
Behind him came multiple entities adorned in Togas, their forms marking them as representatives of something official, something organized.
Paradoxossmiled with both faces as he approached the party of a Primordial Architect, an Undivided One, and a Formless Terror.
Naldine stared at the party coming toward them as she frowned right away.
And without even wasting a second, she spoke words that had ended Civilizations across eons of application.
"Ashes to Ashes, Dust to Dust."
BOOM!

The word |ASHES| instantly hung above Paradoxos and those around him, burning into existence with authority pressing against the crystallized forests around them. Their expressions changed in that instant, confusion and alarm flickering across the two faces of Paradoxos as he recognized what was happening.
But recognition came too late, and their bodies trembled with coldness spreading from their foundations outward as they began to turn to ash!

The Absolute’s form crumbled first, his two faces maintaining their expressions of shock even as the structure supporting them dissolved into gray particles. The Paradoxian entities followed moments later, their disciplined formations breaking apart as each one succumbed to the fundamental truth Naldine had imposed upon their existences.
Her face remained cold throughout, watching the dissolution with eyes holding neither satisfaction nor regret!
Arthur and Gunther before her were astonished, but before either could ask anything, Naldine spoke with a voice cutting through their shock.
"You fools have such poor potential and remain stuck on THE First Scale that you do not sense when an attack is already sent your way."

As she spoke, she waved her hands to reveal a white triangular object with an obsidian eye at its very center. The item radiated an aura of a complete Axiom, and she turned it toward the ashes of Paradoxos and his companions. The gray particles flowed into the obsidian eye like water drawn toward a drain, carrying fragments of the existences they had once comprised.
Naldine focused on the item as its eye opened and began showing illusory scenes playing out above its surface.
They were scenes of...
THE Agora of Primordial Judgment.
She watched Paradoxos standing among three other Strategoi, saw THE Primordial Paradox present among them, and saw THE Youngest.
Memories of him floated from the Axiom and into her mind!
Noah Osmont. The one who laid the Claim to The First Tongue? Was this The Infinity-bearer?
His presence seemed dimmer than expected, his external radiance subdued, and yet something about him made even recorded observation bend slightly.
The scenes passed quickly as her eyes became sharp.

"It seems a unified existence is spreading across Observable Existence, but that is an obsolete concern for beings at our Scale. What matters most is that I have found the one. The one who should be the Guider of Infinity."
The others turned toward her seriously as she said simply, "Let us go. The Infinity-bearer is in THE Agora."

She did not even spare a thought to those she had just collapsed. Even if their weavings could be reversed and cured from the effects of unified definition and undefinition, if one truly lost their Civilization to something like that, they were not deserving of THE Scales of Existence.
The weak Civilizations would be weeded out, and only the strong would prosper in the end.
Naldine waved her hand as she tore existence apart, opening her mouth to speakrubbishthat compelled reality to acknowledge her authority.
THE Interstices opened up in front of them for them to squeeze into, that space between spaces where those who knew how to navigate could travel impossible distances.
Her gaze was cold and imperious as she stepped toward the opening.

She was not looking forward to meeting the Guider of Infinity, and the realization surprised her. She had spent considerable effort tracking this being across Observable Existence, gathering fragments of scattered Infinity and following traces through Primordial Realm after Primordial Realm. Finding him should have produced satisfaction.
But what she felt instead was something approaching fear.

Not fear of the Infinity-bearer himself, for she operated at THE Second Scale and had no such thing. Her fear was different. She was afraid of him not being up to par with the Echoes she had heard, afraid that he would prove merely lucky, merely a being upon whom great power had landed without the wisdom to wield it properly.
Why would the weavings of Infinity fall on something so young? So inexperienced?

She had to determine why. If he proved worthy, arrangements could be made. If he proved unworthy, well. Naldine had never hesitated to remove obstacles from her path, regardless of how much potential those obstacles might have possessed.
She stepped into THE Interstices without looking back, intent on arriving in Ginnungagap, past ite Vaults, and into THE Agora.
Arthur and Gunther followed!

sentences.text: The blue singularities in her white eyes orbited faster, conveying something approaching contempt.
"Sometimes great power can land on those who do not know how to use it.
First, I have to meet him.
If he is worthy, we will see what arrangements might be made.
Until then, you two better not be embarrassments who grovel at his feet just because of Echoes of Causes you heard whispered across the void."
She stepped forward, her presence pressing against both Arthur and Gunther with weight reminding them exactly who led their particular association.
"We ultimately seek Infinity, not just the one who Guides it, however grand they may be.
They are not synonymous with Infinity itself, just those capable of doing much more with it than the rest of us.
The authority matters.
The wielder is merely a obstacle or opportunity depending on how they respond to our approach."
Her cold gaze swept across both of them, demanding acknowledgment of her position.
"Okay?
Arthur, Gunther, are you..."
She trailed off, her attention snapping toward the distance with sharpness that made both her companions turn to follow her gaze.
The blue singularities in her eyes contracted to points of intense focus, and her beautiful features hardened into expression holding neither welcome nor hostility, only assessment.
In the distance, outlines were approaching through the crystallized forests of Alfheimr’s outer fringes.
An Absolute led the group, his form unmistakable.
Two faces occupied a single head, one serene and one severe, both currently arranged into expressions of polite interest.
He floated forward with casual grace, his authority pressing against the environment without demanding submission from it.
Behind him came multiple entities adorned in Togas, their forms marking them as representatives of something official, something organized.
Paradoxossmiled with both faces as he approached the party of a Primordial Architect, an Undivided One, and a Formless Terror.
Naldine stared at the party coming toward them as she frowned right away.
And without even wasting a second, she spoke words that had ended Civilizations across eons of application.
"Ashes to Ashes, Dust to Dust."
BOOM!
The word |ASHES| instantly hung above Paradoxos and those around him, burning into existence with authority pressing against the crystallized forests around them.
Their expressions changed in that instant, confusion and alarm flickering across the two faces of Paradoxos as he recognized what was happening.
But recognition came too late, and their bodies trembled with coldness spreading from their foundations outward as they began to turn to ash!
The Absolute’s form crumbled first, his two faces maintaining their expressions of shock even as the structure supporting them dissolved into gray particles.
The Paradoxian entities followed moments later, their disciplined formations breaking apart as each one succumbed to the fundamental truth Naldine had imposed upon their existences.
Her face remained cold throughout, watching the dissolution with eyes holding neither satisfaction nor regret!
Arthur and Gunther before her were astonished, but before either could ask anything, Naldine spoke with a voice cutting through their shock.
"You fools have such poor potential and remain stuck on THE First Scale that you do not sense when an attack is already sent your way."
As she spoke, she waved her hands to reveal a white triangular object with an obsidian eye at its very center.
The item radiated an aura of a complete Axiom, and she turned it toward the ashes of Paradoxos and his companions.
The gray particles flowed into the obsidian eye like water drawn toward a drain, carrying fragments of the existences they had once comprised.
Naldine focused on the item as its eye opened and began showing illusory scenes playing out above its surface.
They were scenes of...
THE Agora of Primordial Judgment.
She watched Paradoxos standing among three other Strategoi, saw THE Primordial Paradox present among them, and saw THE Youngest.
Memories of him floated from the Axiom and into her mind!
Noah Osmont.
The one who laid the Claim to The First Tongue?
Was this The Infinity-bearer?
His presence seemed dimmer than expected, his external radiance subdued, and yet something about him made even recorded observation bend slightly.
The scenes passed quickly as her eyes became sharp.

What matters most is that I have found the one.
The one who should be the Guider of Infinity."

The Infinity-bearer is in THE Agora."

chapters.title: Chapter 5009: Glorious Purpose! I
paragraphs: In Alfheimr.
On the mountain where THE Creature used to reside, where his multicolored flames had once blazed, a different presence now occupied that space.
The ancient being had departed, leaving behind only the lingering weight of his previous occupation.
One particular lifeform worthy of interest was a woman whose teeth had barely regrown after they were knocked out by THE Youngest not too long ago.

THE Living Emotive sat near an Undivided One, her legs dangling over the edge of a crystallized outcropping as she gazed out across the stretches of Alfheimr below. Her companion said nothing, simply existing in her presence with patience.
The bruises on her face had healed. The damage to her pride had not, though she wore that damage like jewelry rather than wounds.
Everybody underestimated the weak woman of ill repute.
She was just someone who bounced around from one of THE Four to another, right? Just a loose woman seeking protection from whoever would provide it.
Just the Broken Doll who shattered and reformed depending on which powerful being currently found her amusing. That was what they thought. That was what she let them think.
But oh, how little they understood.

She smiled brilliantly, her new white teeth gleaming in the ambient light of Alfheimr’s crystallized forests. The smile stretched too wide, held too long, carried edges that suggested something unstable lurking beneath the surface.
"My big burly Chaos was caught in a web of unity, I sensed it and truly utilized our bond!"
Her voice emerged sing-song and lilting, each word dancing with manic energy.
"The strength of...what is it called now? The Primordial Mycelia! The strength of that little fungus is now draining and flowing into me, filling me up so deliciously!"
She giggled, the sound bright and broken simultaneously.
"Huhu, as I get stronger, I will come back for you, O Youngest. O Osmont!"
Her eyes blazed with something beyond mere interest.
"For you have stolen my heart!"
The Undivided One beside her shifted slightly but offered no comment.
Nobody knew how her power worked.

Even THE Creature had sat her down once and explained how what she possessed was unique across Observable Existence, how she could make something of herself if she chose to apply her capabilities with purpose.

But she had not even told him the true extent of what she could do, had smiled and nodded and let him believe he understood her while keeping the depths of her nature hidden behind eyes that everyone dismissed as empty.
Power was a funny thing, really.

When you hid things about it from all others, when you let them assume you were weak while cultivating strength in shadows they never thought to examine, the things you could accomplish became terrifying. THE Four thought she clung to them for protection. They never considered that she clung to them for access, for connection, for bonds that let her siphon what she needed while appearing to give nothing but companionship in return.
And now THE Primordial Chaos had fallen to THE Entity’s infection.

That warm unity spreading across his existence, that Primordial Mycelia weaving through his foundations, it thought it was consuming him. It thought it was adding his strength to its collective. But the bond between THE Living Emotive and THE Primordial Chaos ran deeper than infection could reach, and through that bond, she was drinking from both of them without either noticing.
None knew that she could tap into and drink from the bond, and she...had always hidden this before and never done it for the past eons.
She licked her new teeth with tongue that savored the sensation of regeneration.
But beyond power, beyond the delicious strength flowing into her existence through channels no one suspected, there was something else occupying her thoughts.

She had never been treated the way THE Youngest had treated her. To slap her like that, without hesitation, without the careful handling that others always employed when dealing with her. To look at her like that, with contempt so pure it bordered on refreshing.
Ah.
She really wanted Osmont.
Not in the way she had wanted THE Creature or THE Primordial Chaos or any of the others she had attached herself to across eons of careful positioning.
Those had been strategic desires, calculated attachments designed to serve her hidden purposes. This was different. This burned with something she had almost forgotten she could feel.
He had looked at her like she was nothing.
And she... wanted to make him look at her like she was everything.
"Wait for me, O Youngest."
Her sing-song voice carried across the mountain as her smile stretched wider still.
"The Broken Doll is putting herself back together, piece by piece by piece. And when she’s whole again, she’ll come dancing to your door!"
In THE Infiniverse.
Noah looked at THE Infinite Root of Uncountable Saturation floating before him, its crystallized blue form existing as both singular and infinite simultaneously.
He was a finite being conducting Infinity.

But he was doing so in a Countable manner, his endless authority flowing through patterns that could theoretically be observed and listed. First, second, third, onward forever. Sequential. Ordered. Limited by the very structure of how he perceived the endless sea he now directed rather than contained.

This was shown by the slight strain he felt sometimes when conducting Infinity across vast distances. The sensation was minor, barely noticeable amid the immensity of what he could accomplish, but it existed. And anything that existed could be overcome. Anything that limited him could be expanded beyond those limits.
So if he used Infinity inside an object to expand what he could do with Infinity...
Noah reached out and grasped THE Infinite Root of Uncountable Saturation.

It felt cold in his palm, cold in the way that endless sequences felt cold, temperature that had nothing to do with physical sensation and everything to do with the nature of what he held. The root pulsed with authority that was simultaneously one and infinite, a single object containing endless instances of itself.
He brought it to his mouth and swallowed.

The sensation of a finite being consuming an Infinite object was...unique. It was not like eating and it was not like drinking. It was like opening a door within himself and allowing something vast to flow through that door into spaces he had not known existed until this moment.
He directed it toward his nature and foundation.

The root’s authority spread through his existence with purpose responding to his will, seeking the places where his Countable Infinity operated and pressing against those limitations with density that refused to accept sequence as the only form of endless expression!
He felt it reaching his Surface Depth, that outermost layer of his Infinite nature where his conducted authority first manifested.
And then the transition began.

One moment, Noah sensed Infinity in the manner he had always sensed it. Sequential points extending forever, one after another, countable if one had eternity to count. The next moment, something shifted in his perception with booming, magisterial violence that made him gasp!
The gaps filled.

Between every point of Infinity he had previously perceived, new points emerged. And between those new points, more points emerged.And between those, still more, infinitely, endlessly, density that could not be listed no matter how one tried because there was always more between any two instances one attempted to identify.
HUUM!
His body rose into the air above the green-gold grasses and golden earth of THE Infiniverse, lifted by forces responding to the transformation occurring within his foundations!
A hymn and soft symphony began to play as radiance unfolded!
He began to spin slowly, surrounded by swirling rivers of endless blue that gathered from all directions to cradle him in their embrace.
The rivers held him with something approaching tenderness!
He felt unfathomably grand in that moment, spinning above the fields where Alexander’s transformation had concluded, suspended in authority that seemed eager to show him what Uncountable truly meant.
"A portion of my existence...my Surface Depth, now feels it."
His voice emerged heavy with realization, each word pressing against the rivers of blue surrounding him.
"That Uncountable nature. That density beyond sequence! THAT density!"
He felt BIG! Fat!

He could sense the difference immediately. Where before his conducted Infinity had flowed in streams, now a portion of those streams had become oceans. Where before he had perceived endless points, now he perceived endless points between endless points between endless points. The expansion of his capabilities was not incremental.
It was categorical!

Even though only one part of his existence currently sensed Infinity in its Uncountable form, that single portion transformed everything he understood about what he could accomplish. He could feel other depths within himself waiting for the same elevation, spaces in his foundation that still operated on Countable limitations while his Surface Depth had broken through.
He needed more roots.

Noah extended his will while still spinning in the skies, still cradled by rivers of Infinity. Another THE Convergent Root of Density Absolute emerged from his storage, the finite Sacred Herb materializing before him with presence that seemed diminished compared to what he had just consumed.
He breathed out.

Endless blue rivers flowed from his breath toward the root, but this time the authority he directed carried qualities it had not possessed before. The Uncountable nature of his elevated Surface Depth infused the Infinity he commanded and exhaled, density filling the spaces between densities filling the spaces between more densities.
The root began to transform.

It crystallized and brightened and pulsed with authority accumulating faster than his previous attempt, responding to weavings born from Uncountable Infinity rather than merely Countable. The light grew blinding, and Noah watched through perception that could now see more than it had seen moments before.
HUUM!
Where one THE Infinite Root of Uncountable Saturation had formed previously, nine now emerged from the transformation.

They arranged themselves in a ring around his spinning form, each one blazing with blue light holding densities that exceeded what his first creation had possessed. These were not simply duplicates of what he had produced before. These were grander, denser, more saturated with Uncountable authority because they had been born from weavings that already understood what Uncountable meant.
Noah reached out and touched one of them.

The sensation confirmed what his perception suggested. These roots were fundamentally more potent than his initial creation, Infinite objects born from Infinite methodology rather than from Countable foundations reaching toward Uncountable expression.
|Elevation Detected|

|Your existence has taken a step further, progressing from the command of Countable toward the command of Uncountable Infinities at THE Surface Depth. This represents categorical advancement rather than incremental improvement. What you perceive now differs fundamentally from what you perceived before this elevation.|
|Other Depths await the same elevation to fully unlock the immensities of your existence. Your Infinite Formless Depth. Your foundations beneath foundations.|

|This path has no framework. All discoveries are being made as progression occurs, and there are many unknowns. Your capabilities are being catalogued in real time as you demonstrate them. What you can accomplish may exceed current predictions.|
|9 instances of THE Infinite Root of Uncountable Saturation have been created through Uncountable methodology.|

|These roots differ from your initial creation. Born from weavings that already possessed Uncountable nature, they carry density exceeding the first root by magnitudes that cannot be expressed through Countable comparison. A single root from this batch provides elevation equivalent to multiple roots from Countable production.|
|Consumption of these roots will accelerate your progression toward commanding Uncountable Infinity across all aspects of your existence.|
Noah read these prompts while spinning in skies filled with endless blue, rivers of Infinity cradling his form. The path forward was obvious. He did not need to contemplate or plan or strategize.
He needed to consume.

Without delaying, he reached out and grasped the nearest root, bringing it to his mouth and swallowing it with the same motion. The Uncountable authority flooded into his existence, seeking his Formless Depth and pressing against its Countable limitations with density demanding transformation.
Then he reached for the second root.
Then the third.
Then the fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth.

Each consumption built upon the previous ones, Uncountable nature spreading through his foundations with momentum that compounded. His spinning accelerated as the rivers of Infinity responded to what he was becoming, their embrace tightening!

chapters.title: Chapter 5010: Glorious Purpose! II
paragraphs: Noah had already experienced many large jumps in power over his journey since he first became a Hunter.

Some of these jumps were ridiculous ones where his entire body would explode or get deconstructed before being built again, flesh and bone and foundation scattered across existence before reforming into something grander than what had been destroyed.
Other jumps left him physically the same but granted him something that fundamentally changed how he perceived existence itself, alterations to awareness rather than structure.
The jump from Countable to Uncountable was a unique one.

His existence did not explode and reconstruct, but he still felt such a significant force of change in how he could potentially wield Infinity compared to before. The difference was categorical rather than incremental, a transformation in the nature of his relationship with the endless sea he conducted rather than merely an expansion of how much he could conduct.
Which in itself was an understatement.

He had not had all that long to experiment with what the major differences would have been at Countable compared to Uncountable since he declared himself a finite existence. The transition had happened too quickly, the Sacred Herbs too effective, the progression too urgent for extended contemplation of each stage along the way.
He almost complained that he was progressing too fast.

As he took the multiple roots, he felt his Intermediate Depth and Fundamental Depths all gain that same irresistible feeling of Uncountable. It felt like most of his finite existence now possessed the sturdier, more immense capability of commanding Infinity. Where before he had sensed endless points in sequence, now he sensed endless points between endless points, density that filled every gap his previous perception had left empty.
If he had been a scrawny thing that could barely lift five pounds, he could now lift hundreds and thousands and even millions of pounds compared to before.

But even that comparison of measurements of weight did not do justice to what he could do before and what he could do now. The difference was not quantitative. It was qualitative, a fundamental shift in the nature of strength itself rather than merely an increase in how much strength he possessed.

The only part of him that remained at Countable was his Absolute Foundation, where his derivative Civilizations of Infinite Hunger and Infinite Undifferentiated Fate resided. But after his change, all of them felt like they were simply part of his greater Civilization, the entanglement and distinction of derivative slowly becoming lost as his existence unified around its new understanding of Infinity.

Because the main Civilization of Mana was not officially at Absolute, it felt like the vast majority of his body was completely Uncountable, and only this one last part remained. He had been keeping it for a grander foundation, waiting for the right moment to elevate it properly. But he knew that Absolute Infinity was too far away, and since the rest of his finite existence had achieved Uncountable...
"Take the step."
HUUM!
He smiled as he commanded his existence to complete the transformation.

The moment he did, brilliance began to unfold within him as he closed his eyes to feel it. His Absolute Foundation trembled and shifted, Countable limitations dissolving as Uncountable density flooded through the last remaining portion of his existence that had not yet been elevated. The sensation was completion, wholeness, every part of his finite being now capable of conducting Infinity in its denser form.
All of him would stand at Absolute, and all of him would be Uncountable!
But he frowned soon after because he sensed something.

Well, another one of his bodies within THE Agora sensed something. Three auras of considerable magnitude were breaching into the Shores of Kleos and moving rapidly toward his location, their approach carrying intent that suggested this was not a social visit.
At such a pivotal moment of his transformation did things have to arise? Could he not simply complete his advancement in peace?
He sighed lightly as his body in THE Agora focused on the approaching presences.
In THE Primordial Archive of THE Agora.

Noah’s seemingly mundane body closed a book that had been shining with stellar obsidian-gold light. The title gleamed across its cover in symbols predating THE Infinite Unfurling: "Architectural Theorems of Scale Transition: Methodologies of the First Primordial Architects."
He had been studying it for insights into what separated THE First Scale from THE Second, seeking understanding that might inform his own unique path.

But he allowed the book to float beside him as he looked up from his research with eyes becoming filled with piercing blue light. He sensed three auras of utmost brilliance breaching into the Shores of Kleos, their trajectory unmistakable. They were coming here, and they were coming fast.
The illusory figure of RUINATION materialized beside him, her blue-gold holographic form flickering into existence with the tragic beauty that characterized her manifestation.
The radiant figure of THE Infiniverse appeared on his other side, multicolored jeweled eyes already focused on the approaching presences with attention.
"Wrap up the devouring of THE Agora."
Noah’s voice emerged calm but heavy with implication.
"It seems we won’t have a moment of peace."

His expression grew serious as he felt the auras more clearly now that they had entered his domain. Two of them blazed with power more terrifying than any Absolute he had encountered. But they should still be at THE First Scale, their authority impressive without crossing the threshold.
The aura of the third was different.

It reminded him of the oppression he had felt from THE Primordial Armor, that crushing weight of someone operating at heights his Scale should not have been able to perceive. The oppression of THE Second Scale. It was likely a Primordial Architect, another ancient being who had achieved what most of existence considered impossible.
Beside him, THE Infiniverse and RUINATION disappeared to work on accelerating their consumption of THE Agora’s resources. They trusted their master to handle whatever approached.
"How do you compare to Beowulf..."

He whispered these words with chilly light in his eyes, genuinely curious whether this Primordial Architect would prove as overwhelming as the one who had nearly captured him in THE Wastes. The memory of that confrontation remained fresh, the sensation of his attacks phasing through platinum armor without effect.
In the next moment, the doors of THE Primordial Archive flung open with brilliance that pressed against the ancient space.
Three vibrant figures appeared in the doorway, and before Noah could fully gaze at them, a sharp and authoritative voice was the first thing that boomed out across the Archive.
"I will have to disappoint. I am not something as simple as Beowulf."
WAA!
The words carried weight that made the Grimoires on their shelves tremble!
With these words, Noah saw them clearly.

An Undivided One in humanoid form stood at the front, his skin shining obsidian beneath clear blue robes, his radiant eyes filled with excitement that seemed inappropriate for the circumstances. Beside him, a Formless Terror whose entire body consisted of crimson tentacles arranged into humanoid shape looked at Noah with similar enthusiasm, as if meeting him was the culmination of something long anticipated.
But Noah’s gaze rapidly focused on the figure floating behind them.
A woman adorned in those same blue robes, but the air surrounding her carried weight of an entirely different magnitude.

Her eyes were pure white with blue dots of singularities orbiting within that whiteness, and radiant white hair cascaded down her back with its own faint luminescence. She was strikingly beautiful and...curvaceous!
Around her, Noah’s eyes opened wide as he could see glimmers of his Infinite Absolute Seals, the ones he had scattered across Observable Existence.
But more than that, silent and calm rivers of Infinity occasionally spun around her form before dispersing.
It seemed minor at first glance, but Infinity was rotating around her and empowering her.

His eyes became sharp as he grasped the floating book in his hands, looking at the new entrants who had not attacked right away despite their dramatic entrance. That hesitation suggested they wanted something other than immediate conflict.
"And what might this be?"
His voice emerged measured, curious despite the tension pressing against THE Primordial Archive.
"An Undivided One, a Formless Terror, and a Primordial Architect are moving together to chase Infinity? What an odd thing to see."
Existence was vast and filled with wonders, but even this combination was something he had not expected.
The Formless Terror and Undivided One were looking at him with shining eyes. Their enthusiasm was almost unsettling in its intensity.

In the next moment, the Primordial Architect behind them moved forward as her power pressed against the surroundings with authority that made THE Primordial Archive itself seem to contract slightly. Her voice boomed out with confidence that brooked no argument.
"We came to see the lifeform playing with forces he does not understand. I am Naldine Manthon, and I have come to make sure that you, Osmont, do not cause the Splintering of Observable Existence."
BOOM!
Noah’s eyes became sharp as the words registered.
What the fuck was this crazy thing talking about?

Naldine stepped forward calmly and imposingly, her pure white gaze sweeping across THE Primordial Archive before focusing on him again with intensity that suggested she was trying her hand in evaluating every aspect of his existence simultaneously.
Her voice continued with the certainty of someone who had spent eons building toward this moment.

"Observable Existence is so vast and stable that even something at THE Second Scale could attack it for eons and it would not crumble. You are weaker than something at THE Second Scale, but you happen to have tapped into a power you barely understand."
Her singularity-dotted eyes narrowed.

"If you are foolish enough, Splintering Observable Existence into Undefinition can only be a matter of time. I have listened to the Echoes of THE First Cause and the Artificial Causes over eons. I have studied Infinity and its wonder and its Encroaching Imperiosus."
She took another step forward, her presence pressing against Noah as Infinity began to gather around him.
"I...bear a weight and purpose even you cannot understand."

chapters.title: Chapter 5011: THE Gamaidjan! I
paragraphs: Noah looked at the Primordial Architect in front of him.

The last Primordial Architect he had encountered had been trying to eat him. His guard remained high, and he was ready to defend and put into practice exactly what Uncountable Infinity could do if this encounter turned violent.
She had come at a critical moment.

His transformation of his main Civilization of Mana to the level of Absolute was occurring right now in his other body within THE Infiniverse, all of his existence shifting toward being fully at the Uncountable Infinity level. The timing was a rather unfortunate coincidence.

But the more time passed, the more he understood exactly what this stage meant for him as a finite being who could command Uncountable Infinities. The density between densities. The endless points filling endless gaps. His capabilities had expanded categorically rather than incrementally, and that expansion changed everything about how he evaluated threats.

So even though a Second Scale Primordial Architect stood before him, he knew he would be able to at least escape if he needed to. THE Infiniverse was already rapidly devouring as much of THE Agora as possible while time passed here, her consumption accelerating in response to her master’s unspoken urgency. Every moment this conversation continued was a moment his forces grew stronger.
If time could pass without conflict, that was ideal.

And the things this Primordial Architect was saying might just be enlightening enough to expand his knowledge, so he would humor her. His eyes shone brightly as he picked up the most important words she had spoken, filing away implications for later analysis.
"I know very well what I grasp, and I know that utilizing it will not in any way cause the Splintering of Observable Existence."
His voice emerged calm and curious.
"But I will humor you and ask what exactly you mean. And what is Encroaching Imperiosus?"
He had left the business of apocalypses behind him.

He was not initiating any apocalypses, not spreading destruction for its own sake, not seeking to unmake the foundations of reality. Observable Existence was so stable that even those at THE Second Scale could not damage it through direct assault.

THE Living Paradox and every single thing he was doing with his spread of corruption across THE Prima Indifferentia did nothing except alter the state of existence, transforming what was there rather than destroying the substrate itself.
Observable Existence remained strong despite all of that.

How could Noah have anything to do with the Splintering of Observable Existence? The accusation seemed absurd on its face, the kind of claim made by beings who feared what they did not understand rather than beings who had actually studied the nature of what they criticized.
As he asked all of this, the figure of Naldine continued to walk toward him. Her commanding presence seemed to want to occupy everything within THE Primordial Archive.
She stopped several paces away from him, those pure white eyes with their orbiting blue singularities fixed upon his form with intensity.
"You stand before a Second Scale Primordial Architect."
Her voice emerged cold and precise, each word chosen with care.

"And even at this moment, you so strongly believe that everything will be okay. That you will somehow survive this encounter unscathed regardless of what occurs. You know nothing of my power or the capabilities of the two fools behind me, and yet your psyche has already deemed that whatever happens here, you will be fine."
She took another step forward.

"You have not accounted for my power, how tremendous it is, or whether I have those even more powerful than myself that I can call down at any second. You simply assume your survival because you are you."
Her singularity-dotted eyes narrowed.
"Overconfidence. A sense of self-entitlement as if everything in existence should be yours or handed to you. A sense of arrogance that whatever happens, because it is you, you will be okay."
Noah eyes shone brightly as he listened.

"Eyes that gaze upon everything as if it is lesser compared to you. As if you are the only thing in existence that matters while everyone else is just playing parts in your story. A self-centered view of yourself and your superiority, as if in all of existence, you alone matter."
Her voice dropped to something approaching clinical observation.
"The inability to admit any faults. The certainty that your judgment is correct simply because it is yours. The assumption that your path is the right path because you are the one walking it."
She paused, letting her words settle.
"Does...any of this ring a bell?"
Noah felt his thoughts buzz as he actually considered what she was saying rather than dismissing it.
Did he think he would survive this encounter? Yes. Had he accounted for her actual power before reaching that conclusion? Well, somewhat.
He subconsciously thought this because of his own power. His own judgment and Intuition that he always relied on. Was that so wrong?
"Your entire being is already so steeped in THE Encroaching Imperiosus of Infinity that you cannot even distinguish your own mentality from its influence."

"You cannot even begin to realize when you started thinking this way. When your confidence became certainty. When your determination became arrogance. When your strength became entitlement. The transition was so gradual and so complete that you believe these thoughts are yours, that this mentality is simply who you are."
Her white hair seemed to glow faintly as she spoke.
"That is THE Encroaching Imperiosus. THE Gamaidjan. The curse and cost that comes with Infinity, which every Second Scale existence playing with it has to be careful of."
She looked at him with something approaching pity beneath her cold evaluation.

"Because more often than not, this is the cost that causes the highest rates of mortality across truly powerful existences. Not external enemies. Not overwhelming force. Not ancient horrors emerging from THE Prima Indifferentia to consume everything in their path."
Her voice hardened.

"Themselves. Their own certainty that they are special. Their own belief that the rules applying to everyone else do not apply to them. Their own arrogance leading them into situations that their power could not extract them from, because they never truly believed those situations were possible."
BOOM!
The revelation pressed against Noah’s awareness. He wasn’t entirely dismissive!
After all, his intuition told him this Primordial Architect was not just making this up.
But...
He found himself actually examining his own thoughts, his own assumptions, his own certainty that he would be fine no matter what.
Where had that certainty come from?
He remembered being afraid. He remembered desperation and uncertainty.
But even then, some part of him had believed he would survive.
Some part of him had never truly accepted the possibility of his own ending.

Was that confidence earned through countless victories? Was that determination forged through adversity that had always, eventually, been overcome? Or was that something else entirely, something that had crept into his foundations alongside the Infinity he conducted?
THE Beholder’s warning echoed through his memory.
Your biggest strength will be Infinity. And your biggest weakness will be Infinity.
Everything comes at a cost. Everything has a cost.
He thought about all of this, but in the end, the thought he arrived to was...no.
No.
He was walking a fine line between confidence and arrogance.
But he knew himself.
He was tyrannical, yes. But he...was alsoquintessential.
So towards the heavy words from Naldine that should have been akin to a grand revelation, he looked at her and smiled brilliantly, and her gaze became even heavier and colder!

chapters.title: Chapter 5012: THE Gamaidjan! II
paragraphs: Naldine saw Noah’s smile and shook her head slowly.
"Did any of what I said go through your head? Or has THE Gamaidjan become so entrenched within you?"
Her voice carried weight pressing against THE Primordial Archive around them.

"Has the madness of Infinity already permeated inside of you so much? You have been the one utilizing it the most, so it would be understandable if you could no longer distinguish between your own thoughts and its influence."

Her calm and powerful eyes shone brightly, eyes that had witnessed eons of existence and the rise and fall of beings who had believed themselves beyond consequence. She looked at Noah as if examining a specimen, searching for signs of infection she was certain existed.
Noah looked at this Primordial Architect as he waved his hands.

Rivers of Infinity began to swirl around his fingers, blue light gathering from directions that should not have contained anything to gather. But this was not the sequential flow he had commanded before his transformation. This was Uncountable in nature, endless points filling the gaps between endless points, density that made his previous expressions seem like trickles compared to floods.
Dense! Dense! Dense!

The rivers quickly transformed into raging torrents, their power ecstatic and eager. They swirled around his hands and arms and shoulders with intensity that pressed against the ancient knowledge stored within THE Primordial Archive, Grimoires trembling on their shelves in response to authority they had never encountered before.

Arthur and Gunther saw this from behind Naldine, and their eyes shone brighter as they came closer. The Undivided One’s obsidian features practically glowed with reverence, while the Formless Terror’s crimson tentacles churned with excitement he could barely contain.
Noah let the rivers rage around him as he spoke.
"You speak of arrogance and self-entitlement. Of eyes that gaze upon everything as lesser. Of certainty that my path is right simply because it is mine."
His voice emerged calm, measured, and had the weight of someone who had genuinely considered the accusation before responding.

"I know the line between arrogance and confidence. I know I am not the center of existence. I have lived for such a short time while existence has been around trillions of times longer than what I have experienced. The cycles before me stretch beyond comprehension, and the cycles after me will likely stretch just as far."
He looked at Naldine directly.

"But even if I know I am not at the center of existence, I can still move and act with confidence. To go through the adversity of existence, one needs confidence in themselves. In their way. In their ability to overcome whatever descends upon them."
The rivers of Infinity around him intensified.
"I have profound confidence that I have not fallen to the madness of Infinity. But hey, maybe I am wrong."
He smiled.
"Is me thinking I could be wrong not also refuting the curse? THE Gamaidjan? I doubt. I fear. I question my own assumptions and examine my own thoughts."
His eyes shone with light that pressed against Naldine’s Second Scale presence.
"But forget all that. Let me ask you this, O Primordial Architect. Naldine Manthon."
He paused.
"Do you fear death?"
BOOM!

The question seemed simple on its surface. Naldine looked at him closely, her pure white eyes with their orbiting blue singularities fixed upon his form with intensity that suggested she was evaluating whether this question deserved a serious answer.
It did.
"Death is nothing to us."
Her voice emerged with the certainty of philosophy refined across eons of contemplation.

"Because when we exist, death is not here. And when death is here, we do not exist. Since pleasure and pain require consciousness, non-existence is neither good nor bad. It simply is the absence of experience, and absence cannot be experienced."
Her white hair seemed to glow faintly as she continued.

"Death is a natural, fated part of existence, like birth. The cycle completes itself regardless of our feelings about its completion. To fear death is to fear the inevitable, and fearing the inevitable accomplishes nothing except poisoning whatever time remains before its arrival."
Her eyes were cold and glorious.
"I do not fear death."
Noah clapped his hands calmly, the sound cutting through the raging rivers of Infinity still swirling around his form.
"Well said!"
His voice carried genuine appreciation.

"I also do not fear death. Not because I believe I cannot die, but because if I do, many who depend on me will face difficulties. My family. My forces. My Civilization. All of them would suffer consequences I cannot permit them to suffer."
He let his hands fall to his sides, the rivers of Infinity calming slightly in response.

"So while I do not fear death, I cannot have it happen. Thus, I move and act with profound confidence because I told myself, and I keep telling myself, I cannot die. Not because I really cannot die. I know I can. But because I know I cannot have that happen. Not just yet."
His eyes shone with purpose that had nothing to do with arrogance.
Death was a unique thing. And even now, Noah had not met anything that could not die. They could live for as many eons as they wanted...but their existences could still be collapsed!
"I have so much to do. So much to learn. So much of Infinity for me to explore and so much of existence to understand. That is why I know I have not gone mad with Infinity."
He looked at Naldine with expression carrying neither hostility nor submission.
"Thanks for your input and information, but it may not truly apply to me."
Naldine looked at him coldly, her expression unchanged by his words despite their logic.
"THE Gamaidjan is never so simple. It would not be so simple in its effects for someone like you. It expresses differently for everyone. "
Her voice dropped to something approaching warning.
"Say, does this ring a bell?"
She began to speak words that pressed against reality itself.

"The Shroud of Endless Blue shall fall upon Observable Existence. It shall be both salvation and damnation, both the key and the lock, both the bridge and the chasm. Under its weight, the doors of the Scales shall open or the doors of the Scales shall shatter. There is no third path. There is no middle ground. There is only the choice that is not a choice."
