chapters.title: Chapter 5013: Echoes I
paragraphs: Her eyes burned with the intensity of someone reciting words they had spent eons studying.
"This is what shall come to pass, for it has already passed, and it shall pass again. The wheel turns. The river flows. The question echoes."
Her voice reached crescendo.
"He shall be the answer, or he shall be nothing. Or he shall be the question that ends all answers."
She had uttered the Echoes Noah had heard some time ago.

Well, not really all that long ago in objective terms, but so much had happened since then. Since his trip from eons ago from THE Prima Indifferentia. Since he had first heard those words and wondered what they meant for his future.
He could not help but smile devilishly as recognition flickered across his features.
"Now, where did you hear that?"
Naldine’s expression remained cold as she waved her own hand in response.

Waves of her power at THE Second Scale erupted from her form, authority that made the raging rivers of Infinity around Noah seem slightly less by comparison. Her grand Civilization covered her existence with a white bubble of light blazing with intensity that spoke of eons of refinement and cultivation.
And that white bubble began to pull a single, silent river of Infinity to swirl around it.

Just one. Not the dozens raging around Noah. Not the ecstatic torrents that responded to his every thought. Just a single river, tugged toward her Civilization with methodology that spoke of careful study.
"I have heard this Echo and more."
Her voice emerged with weight pressing against everything within THE Primordial Archive.

"And I am here to ensure you do not fall to THE Gamaidjan. Because for some fucking reason, you shall be the answer, or you shall be nothing. You shall be both salvation and damnation, as under your weight, the doors of the Scales shall open or the doors of the Scales shall shatter."
Her singularity-dotted eyes blazed.
"For some fucking insane reason, the fate of Observable Existence may rest on whether you maintain your sanity while wielding authority that has driven beings far older than you into madness."
She stepped forward, her white bubble of Civilization and its single river of Infinity pressing against Noah’s raging torrents.
"Help me help you, and there will not be issues. Defy me..."
Her smile was cold and beautiful.
"Well, I have changed plenty of Echoes of Causes myself. I would be itching to give a try to one of the biggest ones."
BOOM!

Her visage was glorious and imposing, and she did not lose out at all to Noah’s brilliance. Two forces pressed against each other within THE Primordial Archive, rivers of Uncountable Infinity meeting a single river pulled by methodology refined across eons.
Noah remained calm as his eyes shone with something new.
Curiosity.
"One of the biggest ones?"
His voice carried genuine interest that had nothing to do with the confrontation pressing against him.
"You know of other Echoes like that from THE First Cause?"
He was curious.
Now, he was really curious.
When an unstoppable force meets an immovable object, what happens?

At this moment in time, there was an extremely old existence that had seen a great deal, asserting something with tremendous confidence born from eons of observation and study. On the other side stood a relatively young existence who was also asserting something with tremendous confidence, the basis of his certainty being one of astounding origin that the old existence could not fully comprehend.
Both believed they were absolutely right.
But both were wise enough to also doubt that there could be a chance they were wrong.

Naldine looked at the entity she had been searching for across Observable Existence, the Guider of Infinity who had scattered his authority so freely that tracking him had become almost trivial once she knew what to look for. At this moment, she chose to extend a careful sliver of the benefit of the doubt.

Her body stopped buzzing with the light of Infinity, the single river she had tugged toward her Civilization dispersing back into the ambient weavings of THE Primordial Archive. The confrontational pressure that had been building between them eased slightly, though neither relaxed their awareness of the other.
"What exactly do you think the Echoes of THE First Cause are?"
Noah took this question calmly. The rivers of Uncountable Infinity still swirled around his form, but they too had calmed from raging torrents to something more measured.
"Weavings of probabilities and possibilities that emerged a number of years ago."
His answer was simple, direct, and based on what he had understood from his limited exposure to such phenomena.
Naldine listened to this before she gazed at his face closely.
"The Echoes of THE First Cause are existence’s self-defense mechanisms."
Her voice carried weight accumulated across eons of study.

"You are right about probabilities. THE First Cause is the emergence of Observable Existence, and at its emergence, it looked ahead to all the Infinite variations of what it could be. Pay attention to that word. Infinite. The variations were Infinite, and from those Infinite variations emerged patterns, possibilities, probabilities that pressed themselves into the fabric of what would come to be."
She paused, letting her words settle.

"The Echoes of THE First Cause tell what could be. No matter how grand your belief in yourself is, the Echoes that may involve you are a small part of the greater whole. But small parts can be significant. A single crack can shatter a foundation. A single choice can redirect a river."
Her singularity-dotted eyes focused on him with intensity.

"The Echoes traverse to those capable of hearing them. There is no specific purpose for this traversal, really. We do not hear them so that we can move in particular directions. But if you do hear them and choose to move, that is your own choice. Because after all, they are all probabilities. Anyone making a move based on an Echo would simply want to steer toward one particular probability compared to others."
She tilted her head slightly.
"Do you want to know of the Oldest Echo I have heard?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5014: Echoes II
paragraphs: Noah’s eyes were radiant as he processed what she was offering.

Did he really come across another old babbler who would talk and talk and talk to reveal things about existence he did not know? He had encountered beings like this before, ancient existences who could not resist sharing their accumulated wisdom with anyone who showed even marginal interest.
Okay old hag, he thought.We love listening to babblers.
So he humored her and asked with genuine curiosity, "What is the oldest Echo?"

Naldine’s expression shifted to something approaching solemnity, her features taking on weight. The blue singularities in her white eyes slowed their orbiting, as if even they recognized the significance of what was coming.
"Listen well, for these words predate most of what currently exists."
Her voice dropped to cadence that felt ancient, each syllable pressing against THE Primordial Archive with heaviness that made even the Grimoires seem young by comparison.
"An Architect shall build a beacon born of strife,
Where adversity becomes the cornerstone of life.
A peasant clothed in rags shall swallow evolution whole,
And through consumption find the fragments of a greater whole.
Architects shall watch from heights where slumber is their throne,
While Cognizances guide in idle patterns yet unknown.
The Source forgotten or remembered, burning dim or bright,
And Infinity shall flicker between the dark and light.
When the leap is made between what is defined and not,
Between the differentiated and the formless thought,
There shall be glory rising, Scales ascending high,
Or there shall be the Splintering beneath an endless sky.
The choice that is not choice, the path that is not path,
The calculation made before the aftermath.
All things return to what they were before they came to be,
Or all things rise to heights that none have lived to see."
BOOM!
When she spoke the words, they felt so unfathomably ancient and heavy that Noah could sense them pressing against his foundations with glory that had nothing to do with Naldine’s personal authority!

These were not her words. These were words that had existed since THE First Cause itself, patterns of probability that had embedded themselves into the fabric of Observable Existence before most of what currently lived had even begun to differentiate.
The rivers of Infinity around him buzzed in response.
Naldine looked at Noah, whose eyes now burned with visible Infinity, blue light blazing from his gaze as he processed what he had just heard.
"Just to knock down your Gamaidjan a bit."
Her voice carried cold amusement.

"Your name and weavings were not even mentioned within one of the oldest Echoes. This is just to check your ego, to tell you that you are not everything. Existence is vast. It was vast before you, and it will be vast after you. Whatever role you play in what is coming, it is a role among many roles, not the singular protagonist you may believe yourself to be."
Noah ignored her last words entirely.

His attention had fixed upon the oldest Echo with intensity that blocked out everything else within THE Primordial Archive. He was repeating it in his mind again and again, each word examined and reexamined as he searched for what he could decipher from its ancient patterns.
All things return to what they were before they came to be, Or all things rise to heights that none have lived to see.
Fuck, that was good!
An Architect shall build a beacon born of strife.
Was that THE Creature? Someone else?
A peasant clothed in rags shall swallow evolution whole.
That felt significant in ways he could not yet articulate. The peasant. The motherfuckin peasant!
This guy had his name in all this so long ago?!
There shall be glory rising, Scales ascending high, or there shall be the Splintering beneath an endless sky.
Glory or Splintering.
Advancement or destruction.
No middle ground.

Noah’s mind raced through the possibilities, through the connections, through the patterns that might link this oldest Echo to the one he knew about the Shroud of Endless Blue. Were they different probabilities pointing toward similar outcomes? Were they fragments of a greater pattern that no single Echo could fully express?
He needed to know more.
He needed to understand what existence itself had predicted since before most of what currently lived had even begun to exist!
Noah’s mind continued racing through the possibilities and connections, each line of the oldest Echo branching into interpretations that led to more interpretations.
Naldine looked at him calmly.
"With any Echo of possibilities, you and I and many others can perceive it differently."
Her voice cut through his contemplation with precision.
"When some hear ’All things return to what they were before they came to be, or all things rise to heights that none have lived to see,’ there are those like me who prefer the rise to heights."
Her singularity-dotted gaze hardened.
"And then there are those who want things to return to what they were."
BOOM!
Noah shook his head and refocused on her as he almost wanted to say, what?
The implication of her words pressed against his awareness with glory that made the oldest Echo seem like preamble.
Naldine continued without waiting for his response.

"Some benefit a great deal from the Splintering. Some want things to return to what they were, as they seek Infinity and a Source you do not even understand yet. They want Observable Existence to unravel back toward undifferentiation, back toward the potential that existed before THE First Cause imposed structure upon chaos."
Her voice dropped to something approaching genuine warning.

"When you announced your Infinity across Observable Existence, you made yourself a target of unfathomable proportions. You fucking just sat there and said hey, I am over here. Just come and fuck me up when you get the chance."
Noah felt the wonder of that truth settle into his awareness.

He had spread his Infinite Absolute Seals across Observable Existence because it served his purposes, because it expanded his influence, because it allowed him to accomplish things that would have been impossible otherwise. Adversity. Adversity! Adversity!
Naldine’s gaze hardened further as she continued.
"Things are never black and white. Good or bad. There are only probabilities, and right now, there are others like me moving to steer probabilities they believe are most conducive to their power."
She paused.
"And there are others even more powerful than me who have already found those named in Echoes. The Peasant. The Architect. Others whose identities I will not speak aloud in a place like this."
Her white eyes blazed with intensity.
"You...need to be very clear where you stand, and you need to get moving."
BOOM!

Just come and fuck me up when you get the chance."
Noah felt the wonder of that truth settle into his awareness.

He had spread his Infinite Absolute Seals across Observable Existence because it served his purposes, because it expanded his influence, because it allowed him to accomplish things that would have been impossible otherwise.
Adversity.
Adversity!
Adversity!
Naldine’s gaze hardened further as she continued.
"Things are never black and white.
Good or bad.
There are only probabilities, and right now, there are others like me moving to steer probabilities they believe are most conducive to their power."
She paused.
"And there are others even more powerful than me who have already found those named in Echoes.
The Peasant.
The Architect.
Others whose identities I will not speak aloud in a place like this."
Her white eyes blazed with intensity.
"You...need to be very clear where you stand, and you need to get moving."
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5015: Magisterial! I
paragraphs: Noah’s eyes were unfathomably bright.

The situation around him became clearer with each word Naldine spoke. There were monstrous beings like her, like THE Primordial Armor, and others who followed their own beliefs to push into existence terrifying probabilities.
Factions operating at scales he had not previously considered, steering toward outcomes that served their purposes regardless of what those outcomes meant for everyone else.
Naldine was saying to get a move on due to this, but even before she arrived, he already was.
The moment his finite existence was declared and he became clearer on his capabilities, he had begun moving to clear the board of his enemies.
THE Entity was being bombarded with Infinity while THE Great Usurper silently attacked from within, Eckert’s Idle Weavings spreading through that warm unity without detection.
And he had taken the step to attain Absolute for all his foundations, paired with Uncountable Infinity, preparing himself to make the decisive move he already knew he needed to make.
He checked his existence as his transformation was almost complete.
So as this occurred, he looked at Naldine sharply.
"So, you need me for the probabilities you want to achieve. I...do not particularly need you."
His voice carried weight pressing against her Second Scale presence.
"You are here to keep an eye on me? Ensure THE Gamaidjan does not overtake me? Does this mean the great Primordial Architect, Naldine Manthon, will be following me?"
The Primordial Architect before him gazed forth with chilly light, her singularity-dotted eyes narrowing at the implication of his words.
"My path is a glorious one that does not involve becoming a follower."
Her voice emerged cold and precise.

"You have your Echoes, I have mine. I look at you akin to a young lifeform with an extremely sharp blade that influences you without your knowing. The things you could cut with this blade are many, and among them are my own weavings."
She paused.
"Thus, if I step in early enough before you cut things you should not, what I want will also be achieved in time. The question becomes whether you will oppose me and make it difficult."
Her white eyes blazed with authority.

"What I need to do is observe and shield you from being used by others as powerful if not more powerful than me, beings who would use you to achieve their objectives of Splintering Observable Existence or other worse thingd. Of returning things to a state that would not be ideal."
Noah smiled brilliantly as he looked at this Primordial Architect.

She wanted to join him, but her pride was too high to frame it as becoming a follower. She had to present it as observation, as shielding, as ensuring he did not cut things he should not cut. The semantics amused him.

But unlike what she believed about THE Encroaching Imperiosus being drenched within him, he was not prideful at all about allowing a Second Scale Primordial Architect to be beside one of his bodies. He could use her as a shield to make things even easier for himself.
Why not?
But of course, he could always try to get more benefits.

He looked at her as he waved his hands, revealing three lotus petals shimmering with blue-gold light. THE Bounded Lotus of Sequential Eternity, one of his Sacred Herbs capable of granting access to Countable Infinity.
"If you take one of these lotus petals, you can have more Infinity flowing through you."
He said the words enticingly, offering power that beings across Observable Existence would have killed to possess.
Naldine did not even look at the lotuses a second time.
She moved away, her eyes wandering to all the books and Grimoires nearby as she began examining the contents of THE Primordial Archive with interest.
"My weavings of Infinity are mine to explore. I will not accept anything from another."
Her voice carried finality that brooked no negotiation.
"You can try your luck with those two fools behind me if you wish."

Noah looked over to the Undivided One and Formless Terror whose eyes were shining brilliantly. Their enthusiasm was barely contained. Where Naldine’s pride prevented her from accepting, these two had no such reservations.
They came forward eagerly as Naldine asked calmly while she began flipping through a Grimoire.
"The weavings of Unity that are permeating throughout. Are such minor things stumping you to need help?"
Her voice carried dismissiveness!

"They are significant enough since they are mentioned in Echoes, but they should not be a major ordeal unless you make it out to be. And the Echoes never have to play out. Remember, they are only the likeliest probabilities, nothing more."

She said such words casually as Noah handed out two lotus petals to float toward the powerful entities before him. The deep voice of the Undivided One emerged with gratitude as he introduced himself properly.
"I am Arthur. The Great Arthur. And I have waited eons to touch true Infinity."
The Formless Terror’s crimson tentacles churned with excitement as he spoke next.
"Gunther. And I share my companion’s sentiment entirely."
Noah nodded toward them before he turned back to Naldine.
"As soon as one last piece clicks into place in the next few seconds, I will be attacking that Unity here and... across time."
His eyes shone with purpose.

"For the sake of just further proving you wrong, I will not act all imperious and grand. I am curious what exactly you can contribute, so even though I do not think I need your help, you can exert your hand. I will let you know when ready."
Naldine listened to this calmly before she closed the Grimoire and looked outside THE Archive.

During their talk, all of THE Agora had been taken apart piece by piece by THE Infiniverse’s relentless consumption. This place, THE Primordial Archive, was the only thing that remained. Everything else had been devoured and integrated into Noah’s forces, resources accumulated while words were exchanged.
The expression on Naldine was a unique one at this moment.

Her cold exterior remained, but barely discernible beneath her terrifying power, there was a sense of relief. She had taken a step toward something that had been weighing her down for a long, long time.

Eons of hearing Echoes and wondering what they meant, eons of searching for the one who would be the answer or the nothing, eons of preparing for a confrontation that might determine whether Observable Existence rose to heights or Splintered beneath an endless sky.
She took in a single breath before she turned back to Noah.
"Anything infected with Unity must be extinguished. You cannot save any."
"So even the Claimer of Chaos, THE Primordial Chaos, needs to die."
BOOM!

Her words were heavy as Noah sensed the changes occurring within Arthur and Gunther, their foundations shifting as Bounded Countable Infinity began integrating with their existences. He responded seriously to her declaration.
"Maybe. Maybe not."
Naldine’s eyes sharpened at his response.
"I collapsed the one you call Paradoxos who was unified with Unity. I peered into its existence and memories before the ash dispersed entirely."
Her voice dropped to something approaching genuine warning.

"What you call THE Entity, THE Primordial Mycelia, should have its origins tracing back to one of the Primordial Architects you need to be cautious of. Its weavings irreversibly bind to the host. Unless their existence is collapsed entirely, there will be a resurgence. The Unity will return. The infection will spread again. This is not speculation. This is what I observed in the memories of something that had been fully consumed."
She revealed heavy news as Noah frowned at the implications.

THE Entity’s weavings were irreversible. THE Primordial Chaos, who had been infected, would need to die for the infection to truly end. There was no cure. There was no reversal. There was only collapse or continued spread.
But...Noah repeated himself while waiting for the final pieces to click into place within his transforming existence.
"Maybe. Maybe not."
BOOM!
He was thinking of THE Great Usurper and other things that even this Primordial Architect did not know!

chapters.title: Chapter 5016: Magisterial! II
paragraphs: Noah was in the middle of beginning to respond to Naldine when he stopped.

His body began to emanate waves of blue and multicolored brilliance that pressed against THE Primordial Archive. The transformation he had been monitoring in his other body within THE Infiniverse had finally completed, and the effects cascaded across all instances of his existence simultaneously.
His Civilization of Mana had stepped into Absolute.

Noah felt the change ripple through his foundations with force that made his previous elevations seem...mild. Even though his existence was finite, even though he had declared himself a conductor rather than a container, he felt a terrifying force and brilliance building within him rapidly. It was colorless and multicolored at the same time, generating itself endlessly from somewhere deep within his finite form.
This was something he was very familiar with.

This was something he had always had with him, something that had been present since his earliest days of cultivation. This was the fundamental force that had carried him through every transformation, every advancement, every impossible leap that should have destroyed him but instead made him stronger.
This was... Quintessence.
But not Quintessence as he had known it before.
|Existential Threshold Achieved|

|With all Depths and Civilizations at Absolute and standing at Uncountable Infinity, your existence has attained the precipice of its brilliance. The finite vessel conducting infinite authority has reached a state of harmony that permits the unlocking of capabilities previously dormant within your foundations.|
|Existential Quintessence Infiniforce has been awakened.|

|This force represents the union of your finite nature with the Uncountable Infinities you now command. Where external Infinity must be conducted from other sources and Observable Existence, Quintessence Infiniforce generates from within your own being. It is yours in a way that conducted Infinity can never be yours, born from the very structure of what you are rather than directed from what exists outside you.|

|You can generate limitless amounts of Quintessence Infiniforce from your body.However, because you are finite, you may only handle a certain amount limited by your Scale. The vessel remains finite even as what it produces approaches infinite. This is not a flaw but a feature, for without limitation, identity dissolves into the endless sea it produces.|

|The immensity of your Quintessence Infiniforce equals the vastness of all regions where you have spread weavings of your Infinity. Every Infinite Absolute Seal scattered across Observable Existence and all other definable weavings of infinity contribute to the density of what you can generate within yourself.You can endlessly produce this force to utilize in conjunction with the Infinity you guide and conduct externally.|

|Critical Capability: Even if you existed in endless Undifferentiation or Undefinition where endless potential or Infinity does not flow, you would be capable of endlessly generating Quintessence Infiniforce to fill the external system you occupy. Your finite existence becomes a source rather than merely a conduit. The only limitation is your finite scope of existence itself.|

|Warning: Meditation and other forms of identity affirmation may be required to ground and stabilize your finite existence when generating beyond comfortable thresholds. The Uncountable nature of your Infiniforce means infinite density between infinite densities, endless points filling endless gaps within your own foundations. Without proper stabilization, coherence may become difficult to maintain. What was termed as Encroaching Imperiosus, THE Gamaidjan, may actually occur.|
Noah felt the changes cascading through his existence with euphoria!
He began to endlessly generate Quintessence Infiniforce, and it shone with multicolored light within him, illuminating his foundations from the inside rather than pressing against them from without.
His body began to shine more and more brilliantly.

His skin took on qualities approaching crystalline, light refracting through his form in patterns of density accumulating beyond what flesh should be able to contain. The finite vessel was producing infinite force, and that production was accelerating with each moment that passed.
Naldine became serious while looking at him.

She did not sense the Infinity he had been using before, that external authority conducted from Observable Existence through his finite form. What she sensed now was different. A different type of Infinity entirely, and it was not something he was conducting from outside himself.
It was generating from within him.
Her singularity-dotted eyes widened slightly as she watched this young existence produce what should have been impossible for anything at THE First Scale to produce independently.
Noah took one hand and filled it with Quintessence Infiniforce.

The limb became multicolored crystalline, light blazing from his palm with density that pressed against THE Primordial Archive’s ancient walls. The force swirled and compressed within his grasp, infinite points filling infinite gaps within infinite gaps, Uncountable in nature and entirely his own.
Then he took his other hand as endless blue waves of Infinity from Observable Existence surged toward it.
The external authority responded to his will with eagerness it had always displayed, conducted by his finite form. This was the Infinity he knew, the endless sea he directed rather than contained.
His eyes burned with light of euphoria as he looked at both hands.
One holding internally generated Quintessence Infiniforce, multicolored and crystalline and entirely his own.
One holding externally conducted Infinity, blue and endless and drawn from Observable Existence.

All his cells were cheering with recognition that something magnificent was about to occur. He could not help but laugh as he began bringing his palms together, drawn toward each other with force that felt irresistible, drawn by all parts of him feeling a sense of euphoria he couldnt explain!
The motion seemed to occur in slow motion.
Naldine’s expression changed rapidly as she recognized what was happening.
"Stop!"

Her voice boomed across THE Primordial Archive with authority at THE Second Scale, power that should have frozen anything at THE First Scale in place. She moved simultaneously, her existence flickering as she quickly transported Arthur and Gunther away from THE Primordial Archive entirely.
Then she took a step forward to stop Noah’s hands.

His palms were approaching each other with momentum that seemed irresistible, two different Infinities drawing together with attraction that exceeded anything Naldine had witnessed in eons of existence!
Naldine grasped both of his hands with grip that should have shattered anything at his Scale.

Her body buzzed with power at THE Second Scale as she roared and pushed, trying to force his palms apart. Her Civilization blazed around her, that white bubble of light straining against the forces drawing his hands together.
But they continued forward.
Endlessly.
Irresistibly.
Her Second Scale authority was not enough to stop the attraction between two forms of Infinity that had never been brought together within a single finite existence before!
And before Noah’s eyes, new words appeared.
|Warning: Unprecedented Event Detected|

|You are potentially causing the emergence of a Miniature Existential Cause. The collision of internally generated Quintessence Infiniforce with externally conducted Infinity within a finite vessel has never been recorded in Observable Existence.|
|The results are unknown if this process is not stopped.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5017: Magisterial! III
paragraphs: Naldine had walked Observable Existence for eons beyond counting.

She had witnessed the rise and fall of Civilizations that current beings considered ancient history. She had studied the Echoes of THE First Cause when most who now lived had not yet begun to differentiate from potential into form.
She had grasped THE Second Scale through methodology refined across cycles that would have crushed lesser existences into forgetfulness.
And she had come here to ensure the Guider of Infinity did not contribute to the Splintering of Observable Existence.
Yet, the first thing he did before her was something that might unravel all of nearby existence.

Her mind processed what she was witnessing with speed that beings at THE First Scale could not comprehend. The attraction between two forms of endless authority that had never been brought together in this configuration.
The irresistible momentum drawing his palms toward each other despite her Second Scale grip attempting to force them apart.
She recognized what would be happening immediately as someone of her stature.. could perceive what would occur in the immediate future alongside the present. And what she affirmed was...
A Miniature Cause.
Something only those at THE Second Scale even knew and understood in theory.

Something that could reshape local reality in ways that echoed THE First Cause itself, producing differentiation or undifferentiation depending on factors that could not be predicted before the event occurred.

Miniature Causes were how Primordial Architects tested theories too dangerous to implement at full scale. They were controlled experiments conducted in isolated regions where the results could be contained.
This was not controlled.
This was not isolated.

This was a young lifeform at THE First Scale accidentally initiating something that could tear apart everything within light years of their current position, and his palms were still moving toward each other despite her grip pressing against them with authority that should have been absolute!
Naldine’s Civilization blazed around her with intensity she had not displayed in eons.
Limitless Existence.

Her path through THE Second Scale had been built upon the understanding that existence itself had no boundaries except those imposed by perception. She had cultivated this truth until it became her foundation, until the very concept of limitation became something she could reject within her domain.
Her Civilization allowed her to interact with Infinity because she had made herself theoretically limitless in nature, capable of touching the endless without being overwhelmed by its scope.
She used that Civilization now.

Her hands were not enough. Her grip was not enough. The attraction between his palms exceeded what simple physical intervention could counter, two forms of Infinity recognizing kindred nature and seeking reunion!
So she smacked one hand back with the full weight of her Civilization.
The blow carried authority at THE Second Scale, Limitless Existence pressing against his Quintessence Infiniforce with rejection that declared this collision would not occur.
His left hand flew backward from the impact, multicolored crystalline light scattering from his palm as the internally generated force dispersed slightly.
But his right hand was still moving forward.

The externally conducted Infinity from Observable Existence was still surging toward the space where his palms would have met, still seeking the collision that her intervention had delayed but not prevented.
Naldine did not hesitate.
She squeezed herself between his palms, her body occupying the space where the Miniature Cause would have emerged.

Her back pressed against his chest as she faced the incoming surge of blue Infinity, her hands reaching out to grasp his arms and force them apart with strength that exceeded what her physical form suggested she possessed.
BOOM!
She was calm.
She was imperious.

Her Civilization of Limitless Existence blazed around her like armor, rejecting the collision by placing herself at its center and declaring that no Cause would emerge through her domain. The blue waves of conducted Infinity crashed against her white bubble of light and scattered, redirected away from the point of convergence she now occupied.

His arms resisted her push with the irresistible momentum that had characterized their approach, but she was at THE Second Scale, and her authority exceeded his regardless of what new capabilities he had just unlocked.
She forced his arms apart with steady pressure that brooked no argument, his left hand pushed away from his body, his right hand pushed in the opposite direction.
The attraction between the two Infinities began to fade as distance increased.
Naldine breathed.
Just breathed.
Simple breaths that grounded her existence after exerting authority she had not needed to exert in longer than she cared to remember.

Her white hair had fallen slightly out of its perfect arrangement, strands clinging to her neck where slight sweat had formed from the effort of stopping something that should not have been possible at his Scale.
And at this time...
Noah felt the sudden euphoria within him slowly die down as the collision was prevented.

He breathed out heavily, awareness returning to normal parameters after the overwhelming sensation of his Quintessence Infiniforce awakening. His cells were no longer cheering. His existence was no longer pushing toward union that his conscious mind had not fully understood.
He saw the back of Naldine before him, her form still pressed against his chest, her hands still gripping his arms to keep them separated.
Her hair was filled with slight sweat, white strands catching the ambient light of THE Primordial Archive in ways that made them seem almost luminescent.
She turned around to face him slowly.
Her movement brought her face close to his, her pure white eyes with their orbiting blue singularities meeting his gaze from distance that would have been inappropriate under any other circumstances.
Her breathing was still slightly elevated, her composure still slightly disrupted from the exertion of stopping a Miniature Cause through sheer force of Civilization.
"Do not fucking start initiating Causes that have unpredictable results right now."
Her voice was low, controlled, and carrying warning that pressed against his awareness with weight befitting someone who had just prevented him from accidentally unraveling nearby existence!
Endless Generation.

This term alone was astounding as Noah looked at the Primordial Architect whose face was inches away from his own. Her pure white eyes searched his gaze for something, and after she affirmed his eyes were cognizant and present rather than lost in the euphoria that had nearly caused catastrophe, she let go of his arms and moved two steps backward.

Noah rubbed the areas on his hands where she had clamped down, the pressure of a Second Scale grip leaving sensations that would linger for some time. He thought about what he had just done, about the irresistible attraction that had drawn his palms together, about the collision that Naldine had prevented through direct intervention.
"A Miniature Cause?"

Naldine looked at him with sharp eyes as she waved her hands. The bodies of Arthur and Gunther returned to THE Primordial Archive, both of their eyes closed as they processed the changes of Bounded Countable Infinity integrating with their foundations. They would be occupied for some time yet.
"Something extremely rare for even those at THE Second Scale to accomplish."
Her voice carried weight befitting the subject matter.

"A Miniature Cause is brought into fruition by the interactions of our Civilizations with Infinity in such a profound way that we can initiate Fake Causes, or Miniature Causes, that try to mimic the endless potential that existed before THE First Cause imposed structure upon chaos."
She looked at him with an evaluation that suggested she was still processing how he had nearly accomplished this accidentally.

"Throw a Miniature Cause at your enemy, and anything could happen. They could be unraveled back into undifferentiation. They could be made grander than they were before. They could simply disappear as if they never existed. You would not know the result until it occurred, and sometimes not even then."
Her singularity-dotted eyes hardened.

"The results are unpredictable by design, for they mimic the unpredictability of THE First Cause itself. But you can bet on everything nearby being erased by the process regardless of what specific outcome emerges."

Her words were heavy ones as Noah thought about that irresistible feeling of bringing together Quintessence Infiniforce with conducted Infinity. The attraction had been so natural, so obvious, as if two halves of something greater had recognized each other and sought union without consulting his conscious intent.

Even at this moment, his body continued to endlessly generate that multicolored Quintessence Infiniforce within him. He could feel his existence rapidly getting more and more immense, density accumulating within his finite foundations as the internal production showed no signs of slowing. His finite body had yet to reach a topping point, and he wondered if such a point even existed or if he would simply keep generating until his Scale itself demanded he stop.

And even when it did reach that limit, he would continue generating Quintessence Infiniforce to fill all of THE Infiniverse at the very least. The internally produced force would flow outward to empower his domain, his forces, and his Civilization.
This energy of endless potential was something he wanted to explore thoroughly.
He wanted to see what it could do when utilized properly rather than accidentally.
So he looked toward Naldine with eyes that had calmed from their previous euphoria.
"I will try not to cause any Miniature Causes for now. But I am ready to continue my assault to clear the board against my enemies."
He paused.
"What will you do?"
Naldine Manthon frowned as she looked at him with stern gaze, her expression suggesting she was genuinely worried he would try to unravel existence again the moment she stopped watching.
"What do you plan to do?"
Her voice held suspicion that had not been present before she witnessed him nearly initiate a Miniature Cause through accident alone.
Noah smiled at the question.
"Well, this one actually involves an attack ranging across time, so I will mess around with the past a bit."
BOOM!

Naldine’s expression became colder as she looked at him as if he already had several screws loose. They had just established how dangerous he could be, how close he had come to erasing everything nearby through the collision of two Infinities within his finite form. And now he wanted to mess with time? Temporal weavings that could destabilize the very flow of existence itself?
She wondered how Observable Existence was not already unraveling if this being was doing all of this just in the brief period she had been present.

Was his power not enough to destroy things in the past? Was he somehow protected by mechanisms she could not perceive? Or was he actually cognizant and knowledgeable of what he was doing, operating within boundaries that only appeared reckless from outside observation?
She looked at him up and down as if gauging which possibility was more likely.
Then she shook her head.

She felt like the first thought was much more supported. This guy seemed to be winging it as he went, stumbling from one potentially catastrophic action to the next while somehow not triggering the consequences that should have followed.
She massaged her temples.
"When... are you planning to go?"
When. Not where.
The question acknowledged that temporal manipulation operated on different parameters than spatial travel, that the destination mattered less than the moment being targeted.
Noah smiled at her phrasing.
"Now for this, a trip to THE Interstices is required."
His eyes shone with anticipation.
"I have got a guy whose entire being is dedicated to time."

chapters.title: Chapter 5018: Time Heist I
paragraphs: In THE Interstices.
Amser Modred had witnessed many things across eons of existence dedicated to the study and stewardship of time.
He had observed beings who believed themselves eternal fade into forgotten memory while others emerged from nothing to reshape the very fabric of reality.
But what he witnessed now made him pause with genuine uncertainty.

A terrifying multicolored glow was blooming within Noah, radiating from his body with intensity that pressed against THE Interstices itself. It was not the blue-gold light of the Infinity that had saved him from THE Primordial Mycelia’s infection. This was something else entirely.
The glow began to fill THE Interstices with presence that made Amser’s temporal currents instinctively contract.
This was not the Infinity he had been granted by this being.
He had multiple different Infinities?

Amser found himself genuinely shocked by the implication. The blue-gold authority that had burned away his infection and bound his Civilization beneath THE First Tongue had been overwhelming enough on its own.

That Infinity alone had exceeded what most beings across Observable Existence could ever hope to touch. And yet here was another force entirely, multicolored and radiant and generating from within the Youngest’s form with density that seemed to have no upper limit.
How many authorities did this young existence possess?

The question unsettled him. He had bound himself to this being out of necessity, trading his freedom for survival when THE Primordial Mycelia had been moments away from claiming his consciousness entirely. He did not regret that choice. But he had made it without fully understanding THE Youngest.
Perhaps no one fully understood him.

As Amser processed these thoughts, Noah raised his head. Those eyes shone luminously with light that combined the multicolored internal force and the blue-gold conducted Infinity into something that pressed against perception itself.
"It is time."
The words emerged with glory that made THE Interstices tremble.
"Time to go back to Ginnungagap at that point where both THE Secretive Eon and THE Primordial Chaos were at the same moment in time."

Amser’s initial shock gave way to seriousness as he rose from his position. His purple temporal currents blazed with increased intensity, responding to the invocation of his domain with eagerness that had not diminished despite his new binding.
Time itself recorded who beings were before infection began.
Every moment of existence prior to contact remained inscribed in time.
If they could reach those moments, if they could anchor infected beings to records of themselves before THE Primordial Mycelia touched them, they could restore what Unity had claimed.
Or so they believed.

Amser had proposed this methodology when Noah first questioned him about how he had kept the infection at bay. Using the past as template to overwrite corrupted present. Reaching backward to pull identity forward from moments when that identity was still intact. It was theoretically sound, and his own survival had proven its viability on individual scale.
But did they still plan to proceed this way?

The specifics mattered greatly when dealing with temporal manipulation. One wrong step could unravel causality chains that would take eons to repair, if they could be repaired at all. His cautious nature demanded clarity before proceeding with something this significant.
Before he could even voice his questions, Noah spoke again.
"We will make it quick. Since we cannot change the past, we would simply be doing something that has already occurred in the past."
His luminous eyes held certainty that pressed against Amser’s caution.

"When I think about how this could possibly be done, it means doing something which would not change how everything unfolded. So Eon and Chaos will still get infected. What I will seek to do is plant seeds of my Infinities within their existence without their knowledge."
Noah’s smile carried weight that made the multicolored glow around him intensify.

"This does not change any of the past, but I can activate those seeds with the identities they had when I placed them eons ago. I can activate them in the current time while they are already infected. We would basically be closing another loop."
He paused.
"And I will not appear there as THE Youngest. I could pull out the identity of THE Tongue Whisper."

The words were heavy with implications that Amser’s temporal understanding immediately began processing. Another closed loop. Another instance of actions in the past that had always been part of the timeline, simply unknown until the moment of their execution.
The methodology was sound precisely because it did not seek to change what had already occurred.
It only sought to add what had always been added.

Amser sighed as he sensed the wonder and immensity of this being he had bound himself to. The Youngest thought in patterns that most beings could not follow, operating with confidence that bordered on recklessness while somehow always landing on solutions that worked within the constraints of existence.
He was ready to go.
But in the next moment, Noah spoke again with casualness.
"Oh, a Primordial Architect wants to tag along to see. Get your temporal weavings ready to go."
What?
A Primordial Architect?
Those esteemed beings from THE Prima Indifferentia? Those ancient existences? Why would one of them be anywhere near the Youngest, and why would he speak of their presence so casually?
Amser did not even finish his thoughts.

In the next moment, a figure appeared nearby with transition so smooth that it seemed reality itself had simply decided she should be there. Her gaze was piercing and calculated, white eyes with orbiting blue singularities fixing upon Amser’s form with intensity that made his temporal currents freeze entirely.
Shock flooded through him.
Then horror.
This was a being at THE Second Scale.

Her aura was suffocating in ways that had nothing to do with hostile intent, simply the natural pressure of someone operating at heights so far above his own that comparison became meaningless. Her eyes felt like they were seeing through everything, through his temporal weavings, through his foundations, through every secret he had accumulated across eons of existence.
Someone at THE Second Scale!
THE Youngest had such a thing just waiting beside him?!
Amser’s cautious nature screamed warnings that he could not fully process!
What exactly had he become part of?!

He forced his shock down through discipline refined across eons of temporal stewardship. Panic would accomplish nothing. Questions would have to wait. Right now, he needed to present himself appropriately before a being who could collapse his existence with casual effort.
"I am Amser Modred. THE Living Temporal."

His voice emerged with steadiness that did not reflect his internal turmoil, his introduction carrying the weight of his ancient standing despite his awareness that it meant little before someone at her Scale.
"I...serve THE Youngest and will be facilitating our temporal traversal."
Naldine looked at him with an expression that revealed nothing of her thoughts.
She nodded once.
That was all.
Amser felt like he was on pins and needles in the silence that followed, the pressure of her presence pressing against his temporal currents with weight that made concentration difficult.
He turned away with deliberate slowness, refusing to let his discomfort show more than it already had.
Purple rivers of light bloomed around his form as he prepared to take all three of them to a time he had visited before.

A time after THE Youngest had seemingly escaped from the grasp of himself and THE Primordial Chaos. A time when THE Secretive Eon had been present without anyone except THE Creature knowing she was there.
A time that was about to receive visitors who... had always been there.

His Quintessence Infiniforce pressed against the temporal weavings with weight that made him an active participant rather than passive passenger, his will shaping their trajectory alongside THE Living Temporal’s expertise.
They moved through spaces between moments, through gaps in the fabric of time that only those with temporal authority could perceive.

THE Interstices twisted around them as eons compressed into instants and instants stretched into eternities. Noah felt the sensation of moving backward through existence itself, causality flowing in reverse around his protected consciousness while his destination drew closer with each moment that was not quite a moment.
And then they arrived.
HUUM!
The Primordial Genesis Shore materialized around them with violence that pressed against Noah’s awareness.
They had appeared at that pivotal point in time, a nanosecond after his old self had completed temporal traversal and vanished from this era entirely.
THE Primordial Chaos stood in the distance with expression of frustrated amusement, his hand still extended toward the space where Ul’moreth had been moments before.

The apex entity’s chaotic authority churned around him with intensity that made the nearby Ginnu Lifeforms instinctively retreat, his attention fixed on the skies where THE Creature’s massive titanic form still blazed with multicolored flames.
And THE Living Temporal stood frozen mid-motion, his purple temporal currents flickering strangely.

Noah watched as Amser’s future consciousness settled into his past body, those ancient eyes filling momentarily with awareness that had not existed in them a heartbeat before. The transition was seamless to outside observation, the past version of THE Living Temporal simply pausing as if reconsidering his next action.
But Noah knew what was actually occurring.
His own body looked nothing like the form he usually wore.

He was tall and slender now, with wings unfurled behind his back in configurations of linguistic authority made manifest. His entire existence was surrounded by letters of THE First Tongue, Phonemes orbiting his form in patterns that declared him something ancient and unknowable.
He was THE Tongue Whisperer, an identity he had used before, a mask that concealed the truth of what he had become!

Beside him, Naldine’s blue robe had extended to form a hooded configuration that obscured her features entirely. One could barely perceive her presence at all, her weavings working to minimize her impact on this moment in time!
She was a ghost beside him, a shadow that should not have been able to exist at THE Second Scale without warping reality around her presence.

Below them, shocked and horrified Ginnu Lifeforms scattered across The Primordial Genesis Shore in various states of consciousness. Many had fallen from the skies when THE Creature first appeared, their foundations too weak to withstand even the passive pressure of that apex entity’s manifestation. Others stumbled about in confusion, trying to process the chaos that had just unfolded.
And in the skies above, THE Creature remained.

That massive titanic form surrounded by multicolored flames of pure Existence, heat and steam emanating continuously from features that could not be clearly observed. The being who had clenched his fist and shattered THE Living Temporal’s restraints to allow Noah’s escape. The entity whose intervention had changed everything!
THE Creature’s gaze, filled with flames that burned in impossible colors, briefly looked over toward their position.
Noah’s veiled figure turned his gaze upward and met those burning eyes directly.
So this being had known about them appearing as well?
The realization settled into Noah’s awareness without surprise. THE Creature operated at heights that many found difficult to comprehend!
Of course he would sense temporal manipulation occurring within thid place!
Oh well.
It changed nothing about what needed to be done.

At this time, Noah prepared to move as he had already discussed with Naldine. He was curious to see the power of this Second Scale Primordial Architect in action, curious whether her methodology would prove as effective as she claimed.
Her words rang out in his mind.

"I will freeze everything and everyone here into a Limitless Instant. Infuse your seed of Infinity in those you want during that time, and we will leave right after. We cannot linger or we risk unraveling the temporal weavings of existence."
She said this simply, as if freezing apex entities and ancient horrors into suspended animation was something minor! One must not forget, she was a Primordial Architect at THE Second Scale!

Noah spread his senses outward to find one being in particular, his awareness extending across The Primordial Genesis Shore with perception enhanced by Quintessence Infiniforce that continued generating within him.
He searched among the Ginnu Lifeforms, among the chaos and confusion, looking for someone who should not have been there at all.
An instant later, his eyes brightened.

In a corner between recovering Ginnu Lifeforms, inconspicuously positioned where no one would think to look, he found a curious figure watching the distant confrontation between THE Primordial Chaos and THE Living Temporal with attention.
THE Secretive Eon.
She was there, just as she had said!

Present at this moment without anyone except THE Creature knowing she existed. The attacking point of THE Primordial Mycelia’s infection, the being whose restoration could potentially unravel everything THE Entity had accomplished across Observable Existence.
With all the pieces in place, Noah’s eyes shone brilliantly beneath his disguise as THE Tongue Whisperer.
"Let us go."
HUUM!
He spoke lightly, and utter brilliance began to unfold silently around them!

chapters.title: Chapter 5020: Euphoria I
paragraphs: Noah breathed in and out as he came to realize a problem.

Every time he breathed, every time his existence continued endlessly generating Quintessence Infiniforce, that feeling of euphoria that had built up until he almost brought his hands together to unintentionally cause a Miniature Cause was returning. It crept through his foundations with warmth that made his cells sing and his awareness sharpen to edges that cut against perception itself.
It was as if his existence naturally entered that profound state of euphoria the more Quintessence Infiniforce he generated.

While it was not bad per se, Noah could not quite put his finger on exactly what it meant. Was this THE Gamaidjan that Naldine had warned him about? Was this the madness of Infinity creeping into his consciousness through internal generation rather than external conduction?
Or was this simply what it felt like to be a finite existence producing infinite force, the natural high of something unprecedented occurring within his foundations?
He was not averse to this euphoria.

It caused his existence to buzz in an always ready state, prepared for action at any moment, eager to demonstrate what Quintessence Infiniforce could accomplish when properly directed. The sensation was addictive in ways that his cautious mind recognized as potentially dangerous, but his tyrannical nature embraced as simply the feeling of power that belonged to him.
To the extent that in the next moment, when Naldine raised her hand slightly as if pointing to existence itself, Noah felt ready for absolutely anything.
"Freeze."
HUUM!
A single word from the Second Scale Primordial Architect.

But that single word carried weight that pressed against reality itself with authority accumulated across eons of cultivation. Her Civilization of Limitless Existence declared that this moment would not end, that time would not progress, that everything within her domain would remain suspended in an instant that had no duration.
The color white permeated over everything.

It spread from Naldine’s extended hand like frost across glass, racing outward to touch every surface and every existence within The Primordial Genesis Shore. Ginnu Lifeforms froze mid-motion, their expressions locked in whatever emotion they had been displaying when the effect reached them. THE Living Temporal’s past body became still, purple rivers of time crystallizing into motionless streams. THE Primordial Chaos himself froze with expression of frustrated amusement locked onto his features, his chaotic authority suspended in configurations that should have been impossible to halt.
All bodies became frozen in that Limitless Instant.
All except one.

In the far distance, the multicolored flames surrounding THE Creature were about to be frozen when they blazed brighter with defiance that exceeded even Naldine’s Second Scale authority. The massive titanic form remained in motion while everything else became still, those burning eyes looking down at the scene below with awareness!
Noah affirmed this with shining eyes as he moved.

He appeared instantly before the invisible figure of THE Secretive Eon, crossing distance that should have required measurable time in a moment that existed outside of time entirely. She stood frozen like everything else, her dark hair cascading around features that held natural beauty and grace despite the weight of what she would eventually become.

Her dark eyes were locked on the distant confrontation between THE Primordial Chaos and THE Living Temporal, unaware that she was being observed by someone who knew exactly what infection would be within her foundations eons from now!
Noah pushed his hand forward.

It held a vibrant multicolored singularity filled with Quintessence Infiniforce, internally generated authority compressed into a point of density that exceeded what most beings could produce through any methodology. The singularity sank into her existence silently, passing through her frozen form without resistance, embedding itself deep within foundations that did not yet know they would need restoration.
A seed planted in the past that would bloom in the future.

He then looked over to the other direction where Temporal stood close to THE Primordial Chaos, the past self frozen in proximity to the apex entity who had been grasping Ul’moreth moments before. Noah pointed toward Temporal as vibrant blue weavings of his conducted Infinity flowed from the frozen Absolute, forming a dazzling singularity that floated through the air with purpose that defied the frozen state of everything around it.
The singularity entered the body of THE Primordial Chaos without disturbing his frozen form.

Both singularities now burned with Infinities within their hosts, albeit two different types. The multicolored Quintessence Infiniforce within THE Secretive Eon. The blue conducted Infinity within THE Primordial Chaos. These Infinities could easily mimic the authority of their hosts’ Civilizations and remain dormant for eons, undetectable until the moment Noah chose to activate them.
Until he completed this attack in the present by awakening seeds planted in the past.

Naldine looked over in his direction as if to confirm he was done, her hooded form barely perceptible even to his enhanced awareness. He nodded with bright eyes, mission accomplished, objectives achieved, another closed loop in the making.
But that euphoria from endless generation continued building within him.

It demanded release. It wanted to flourish. It pressed against his finite foundations with force that felt irresistible, similar to how his hands had been drawn together before Naldine stopped him from causing a Miniature Cause.
He wanted to unleash this euphoria.
He wanted to allow Quintessence Infiniforce to flourish and demonstrate what it could do when properly expressed.
But how?
His eyes were bright with possibilities as Naldine sent him a message through their established connection.
"Alright, let us go."
She was saying this.
She was right to say this.

They had accomplished their objectives. The temporal traversal could end now. This could be the shortest journey through time he had ever undertaken, a surgical strike that planted seeds without disturbing the soil of history.
But Noah continued to feel that budding euphoria building within his existence.

With bright eyes shining beneath his disguise as THE Tongue Whisperer, he looked toward THE Creature in the distant skies. That massive titanic form surrounded by multicolored flames, the only existence besides themselves that remained unfrozen in this Limitless Instant.
"Everything that happened in the past has already happened."
His eyes shone with multicolored light of Quintessence Infiniforce as he began to rise from his position, ascending toward the skies with purpose that had nothing to do with their mission objectives.
Naldine frowned as she sensed what he was about to do.

Before she could say anything, before she could warn him about destabilizing temporal weavings or causing unpredictable results, Noah listened to his euphoria. He looked toward the distant figure of THE Creature with eyes blazing and smile spreading across his disguised features.
"Hey! Can we spar?!"
HUUM!
Incredulous words echoed from him across the frozen landscape of The Primordial Genesis Shore.

THE Creature looked down from his position in the skies, those burning eyes analyzing the figure rising toward him. A young existence challenging an apex entity whose passive pressure alone could collapse weaker beings into unconsciousness.
After an instant of consideration, THE Creature gave a light nod.
Noah smiled brilliantly and laughed with genuine delight.

The endlessly generating Quintessence Infiniforce churned within him even more wildly as he shot upward like a bullet, his disguised form blazing with multicolored light that pressed against the frozen reality around them!

Naldine’s expression became colder beneath her hood as she watched this young lifeform ascend. At this time, the effect of freezing everything ended, her Civilization of Limitless Existence releasing its hold on this moment as continuing to maintain it while Noah engaged THE Creature would have been pointless.
The Limitless Instant concluded.
Time resumed.
And to the perspectives of all others present on The Primordial Genesis Shore...
BOOM!

An entity with multicolored brilliance instantly emerged in the skies, shooting out with a heartshaking aura toward THE Creature himself. The frozen moment they had not known they were experiencing simply became a moment like any other, and suddenly there was something new happening that demanded their attention.
Ginnu Lifeforms across the settlement looked upward with shock and confusion.
THE Primordial Chaos turned his gaze skyward with expression shifting from frustrated amusement to genuine curiosity.
THE Living Temporal’s past self looked up with awareness that his future consciousness still occupied, watching events unfold that he now understood had always been part of this moment.
THE Living Origin and THE First Hunger, who had been rushing forward moments before, paused to observe the new development with expressions of complete bewilderment.

Many focused on the ascending figure’s form, on the wings unfurled behind his back, on the letters of THE First Tongue orbiting his existence in patterns that declared ancient authority. Recognition sparked across multiple faces simultaneously.
A Fundamental Depth Ginnu Lifeform voiced out with shock that pressed against his words.
"Is that... THE Tongue Whisperer?!"

THE Tongue Whisperer had appeared again after so long, that mysterious entity who had been immortalized in THE Agora of Primordial Judgment as the one who reached the level of Polemarch as soon as he entered. The being whose origins remained unknown, whose power exceeded his apparent classification, whose presence here made no sense given the circumstances.
And astonishingly, his brilliance smashed toward THE Creature with intent that bordered on madness!

chapters.title: Chapter 5021: Euphoria II
paragraphs: THE Creature!

This was an entity of legends that Noah had begun hearing about when he first started mixing with Foldless Ones across Observable Existence. An entity that was literally a legend, a being from whom the Stories of The Earliest Folds were made, whose very existence had shaped the foundations of reality in ways that most current beings could not comprehend.
He always seemed so far out of reach.
Even when Noah talked with him not long ago in objective time, even when THE Creature had answered his questions and provided insights, that apex entity had felt distant. Untouchable.
And as much as this was THE Creature eons ago, this was still THE Creature.

A Primordial Architect who had shattered what he was to become something beyond classification entirely. Horus called him a Defector. Every being who mentioned him did so with weight that acknowledged his position at the apex of what currently existed.
And now Noah was flying toward him with fist raised and euphoria demanding release.
Generate. Generate. Generate!

His existence buzzed with excitement as boundless Quintessence Infiniforce generated within him, filling his foundations with density that continued expanding without apparent limit. He gathered it all into his hands, concentrating that multicolored internal authority into his fist as he shot upward with speed that pressed against the fabric of this era.
He threw out his punch, trying to release some of his euphoria through the purest expression of intent he could manage.
THE Creature looked down at Noah with shining eyes that burned behind those multicolored flames of Existence.
There was no anger in that gaze. No offense taken at being challenged. If anything, those burning eyes held something approaching curiosity, perhaps even amusement at being asked to spar.
THE Creature stretched his hand back, winding up his own strike with deliberate slowness that made the gesture feel ritualistic.
Then he threw out a fist filled with Existence itself.
HUUM!
Noah looked up as everything seemed to slow down around him.

That punch from THE Creature felt like the weight of all Existence. All Observable Existence contained in that glorious multicolored fist, compressed into an impact that would reshape whatever it touched. The authority behind that strike exceeded anything Noah had ever faced, somehow exceeding even the crushing presence of Beowulf’s Second Scale methodology.
How? How could that be possible? Here, THE Creature should be much weaker!
All of its weight was crushing onto him.
It was suffocating.

The pressure of that approaching fist made his finite existence scream warnings that his conscious mind acknowledged and then promptly ignored. Every instinct told him to flee, to dodge, to do anything except meet that strike head-on with his own power.
And yet he felt an unbelievable thrill coursing through his foundations.

His Quintessence Infiniforce roared and buzzed with intensity and confidence that approached the euphoria he had felt before almost causing a Miniature Cause. It generated boundlessly within him, responding to the challenge with eagerness that matched his own excitement. His finite existence was producing infinite force, and that force demanded expression against the most worthy opponent he could find.
He surged forward with fist blazing multicolored brilliance.
The two fists neared each other across distance that compressed into nothing!
And...!
"I told you not to cause Miniature Causes!"

The booming shout of Naldine Manthon echoed across existence from somewhere below, her Second Scale authority pressing against the scene with desperate intent. She had seen what was about to happen. She had recognized the convergence of forces that should not have been converging. She had tried to stop it!
But she was too late.
In the next moment, two fists met.
HUUM!

At the point of impact, an incandescent white light bloomed between Noah’s multicolored brilliance and THE Creature’s fist of Existence. The light was blinding in ways that transcended mere luminosity, pressing against perception itself with weight that exceeded what eyes were designed to process.

Below, THE Primordial Chaos turned his gaze away with expression of genuine shock, his chaotic authority instinctively shielding his awareness from the brilliance erupting above. THE Living Temporal’s past body flinched backward, purple rivers of time churning with agitation at something that should not have been possible at this Scale. THE Living Origin and THE First Hunger covered their eyes with hands that trembled despite their power.
Even the Ginnu Lifeforms who had already been struggling to comprehend events cried out in pain as that white light seared across their perception.
The light covered everything.

It expanded from the point of impact to encompass the skies above The Primordial Genesis Shore, washing over reality with brilliance that made the multicolored flames of THE Creature seem dim by comparison. For a single eternal instant, nothing existed except that white radiance.
And then Noah and THE Creature disappeared.
Simply gone.

The white light faded as quickly as it had bloomed, leaving behind skies that were suddenly empty of both combatants. No trace remained of the collision. No residual energy marked where two fists had met. They had simply ceased to exist in this moment, removed from this point in time by forces that the observers below could not comprehend.

THE Primordial Chaos stared at the empty sky with expression that had shifted from shock to something approaching genuine concern. His chaotic authority churned around him with agitation that showed even he did not understand what had just occurred.

THE Living Temporal’s past body looked upward with eyes that held awareness his future consciousness provided, understanding that this event had somehow always been part of the timeline while simultaneously being something unprecedented.
THE Living Origin lowered her hands from her eyes with expression of complete bewilderment and concern, her authority flickering with uncertainty that she rarely displayed.

The figure of Naldine Manthon stood among the chaos below, breathing slowly as if calming herself. Her hooded form was barely perceptible, her Civilization of Limitless Existence still working to minimize her presence in this era.
A moment later, she disappeared as well.

But all those who remained on The Primordial Genesis Shore had witnessed what occurred. They had seen THE Tongue Whisperer emerge from nowhere with multicolored brilliance that exceeded anything they had observed from him before. They had watched him challenge THE Creature to single combat. They had observed that apex entity accept the challenge and throw his own strike.
And they had seen both of them vanish in white light that seared itself into their memories.
The Tongue Whisperer had impacted with THE Creature.
And both of them had disappeared.
Who the fuck had won that impact?!

sentences.text: THE Creature!
This was an entity of legends that Noah had begun hearing about when he first started mixing with Foldless Ones across Observable Existence.

An entity that was literally a legend, a being from whom the Stories of The Earliest Folds were made, whose very existence had shaped the foundations of reality in ways that most current beings could not comprehend.
He always seemed so far out of reach.
Even when Noah talked with him not long ago in objective time, even when THE Creature had answered his questions and provided insights, that apex entity had felt distant.
Untouchable.
And as much as this was THE Creature eons ago, this was still THE Creature.
A Primordial Architect who had shattered what he was to become something beyond classification entirely.
Horus called him a Defector.
Every being who mentioned him did so with weight that acknowledged his position at the apex of what currently existed.
And now Noah was flying toward him with fist raised and euphoria demanding release.
Generate.
Generate.
Generate!
His existence buzzed with excitement as boundless Quintessence Infiniforce generated within him, filling his foundations with density that continued expanding without apparent limit.
He gathered it all into his hands, concentrating that multicolored internal authority into his fist as he shot upward with speed that pressed against the fabric of this era.
He threw out his punch, trying to release some of his euphoria through the purest expression of intent he could manage.
THE Creature looked down at Noah with shining eyes that burned behind those multicolored flames of Existence.
There was no anger in that gaze.
No offense taken at being challenged.
If anything, those burning eyes held something approaching curiosity, perhaps even amusement at being asked to spar.
THE Creature stretched his hand back, winding up his own strike with deliberate slowness that made the gesture feel ritualistic.
Then he threw out a fist filled with Existence itself.
HUUM!
Noah looked up as everything seemed to slow down around him.
That punch from THE Creature felt like the weight of all Existence.
All Observable Existence contained in that glorious multicolored fist, compressed into an impact that would reshape whatever it touched.
The authority behind that strike exceeded anything Noah had ever faced, somehow exceeding even the crushing presence of Beowulf’s Second Scale methodology.
How?
How could that be possible?
Here, THE Creature should be much weaker!
All of its weight was crushing onto him.
It was suffocating.
The pressure of that approaching fist made his finite existence scream warnings that his conscious mind acknowledged and then promptly ignored.
Every instinct told him to flee, to dodge, to do anything except meet that strike head-on with his own power.
And yet he felt an unbelievable thrill coursing through his foundations.
His Quintessence Infiniforce roared and buzzed with intensity and confidence that approached the euphoria he had felt before almost causing a Miniature Cause.
It generated boundlessly within him, responding to the challenge with eagerness that matched his own excitement.
His finite existence was producing infinite force, and that force demanded expression against the most worthy opponent he could find.
He surged forward with fist blazing multicolored brilliance.
The two fists neared each other across distance that compressed into nothing!
And...!
"I told you not to cause Miniature Causes!"
The booming shout of Naldine Manthon echoed across existence from somewhere below, her Second Scale authority pressing against the scene with desperate intent.
She had seen what was about to happen.
She had recognized the convergence of forces that should not have been converging.
She had tried to stop it!
But she was too late.
In the next moment, two fists met.
HUUM!
At the point of impact, an incandescent white light bloomed between Noah’s multicolored brilliance and THE Creature’s fist of Existence.
The light was blinding in ways that transcended mere luminosity, pressing against perception itself with weight that exceeded what eyes were designed to process.
Below, THE Primordial Chaos turned his gaze away with expression of genuine shock, his chaotic authority instinctively shielding his awareness from the brilliance erupting above.
THE Living Temporal’s past body flinched backward, purple rivers of time churning with agitation at something that should not have been possible at this Scale.
THE Living Origin and THE First Hunger covered their eyes with hands that trembled despite their power.
Even the Ginnu Lifeforms who had already been struggling to comprehend events cried out in pain as that white light seared across their perception.
The light covered everything.

It expanded from the point of impact to encompass the skies above The Primordial Genesis Shore, washing over reality with brilliance that made the multicolored flames of THE Creature seem dim by comparison.
For a single eternal instant, nothing existed except that white radiance.
And then Noah and THE Creature disappeared.
Simply gone.
The white light faded as quickly as it had bloomed, leaving behind skies that were suddenly empty of both combatants.
No trace remained of the collision.
No residual energy marked where two fists had met.
They had simply ceased to exist in this moment, removed from this point in time by forces that the observers below could not comprehend.
THE Primordial Chaos stared at the empty sky with expression that had shifted from shock to something approaching genuine concern.
His chaotic authority churned around him with agitation that showed even he did not understand what had just occurred.

THE Living Temporal’s past body looked upward with eyes that held awareness his future consciousness provided, understanding that this event had somehow always been part of the timeline while simultaneously being something unprecedented.
