chapters.title: Chapter 5022: The Pluvial Epoch! I
paragraphs: White brilliance surrounded Noah completely.
He could not see THE Creature. He could not see The Primordial Genesis Shore below. He could not see Naldine or Amser or anyone else who had been present at that pivotal moment in time.
There was only endless white light pressing against his awareness from every direction, the aftermath of two fists meeting in collision that should not have occurred.
And prompts began materializing before his vision.
|Miniature Cause Initiated|

|The collision of internally generated Quintessence Infiniforce with externally expressed Existence has triggered a Miniature Cause. This event mimics THE First Cause on localized scale, producing effects that will reshape the region of Observable Existence most saturated with your Infinite authority.|

|Because your weavings are most present in your native era rather than this temporal location, the effects will manifest upon your return to present time. The Miniature Cause has been seeded. Its emergence awaits your arrival.|
Noah’s eyes widened as he processed these initial prompts, but more continued appearing with relentless progression.
|Miniature Cause Effect Classification: The Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity|

|Upon return to present era, endless rainfall of Existential Infinity shall descend across all regions where your Infinity has spread. This rainfall will persist for duration equivalent to 1-2 million years of subjective experience, though objective time may compress or expand depending on local temporal conditions.|
|The rainfall carries the combined authority of your Quintessence Infiniforce and THE Creature’s Existence, merged through Miniature Cause into precipitation that reshapes whatever it touches.|
The prompts continued with weight that made his foundations tremble.
|Primary Effects of the Pluvial Epoch:|

|Cleansing Waters: The rainfall of Existential Infinity is fundamentally incompatible with corruption, infection, and unauthorized unity. Any weavings of corrupted proto-matter of THE Living Paradox, THE Primordial Mycelia, or any similar authorities will be dissolved upon contact with these waters. The rainfall will cleanse Observable Existence to your definition and THE Creature’s definition.|

|This cleansing is not selective. Beings whose foundations have been too thoroughly integrated with corruption may be dissolved alongside the corruption itself. The rainfall does not distinguish between host and infection once merger has progressed beyond recoverable thresholds.|
BOOM!
Noah felt the weight of that warning pressing against his awareness.
The prompts continued without pause for his concern.

|Extinction Event: Weaker Civilizations across regions touched by your Infinity will face existential pressure from the Pluvial Epoch.Those whose foundations cannot withstand prolonged exposure to Existential Infinity rainfall will collapse, their weavings dissolved back into undifferentiated potential. Estimated dissolution rate: approximately one-third to one-half of all Civilizations currently operating within affected regions.|

|This is not destruction. This is acceleration of natural selection applied at Civilizational scale. Those too weak to survive the rainfall were too weak to survive the coming conflicts regardless. The Pluvial Epoch merely advances their inevitable conclusion.|
Noah breathed heavily as he absorbed the scope of what he had triggered.
Mass extinction of Civilizations!
Dissolution of beings who could not withstand the pressure. An event that would reshape Observable Existence on scale that rivaled THE Living Paradox if not exceeding what he did!
Oh!
But the prompts were not finished.

|Evolutionary Radiation: Following the initial cleansing and extinction phases, the Pluvial Epoch will trigger rapid emergence of new Civilizations, new methodologies, and new paths of advancement. The rainfall carries seeds of potential that will take root in foundations strong enough to survive the initial deluge.|

|Beings who endure the Pluvial Epoch will find their Civilizations enhanced by prolonged exposure to Existential Infinity. Their foundations will be saturated with authority that previously required eons of cultivation to accumulate. The survivors will emerge fundamentally transformed, their potential elevated beyond what normal progression could achieve.|

|New classifications of existence may emerge from this transformation. The Pluvial Epoch cultivates. It prepares the soil of Observable Existence for growth that could not occur without first clearing what currently occupies that soil.|

|Climate Restructuring: The water cycle of Existential authority across affected regions will be permanently reorganized. Infinity will flow through channels that did not exist before the Pluvial Epoch, creating new pathways for advancement and new obstacles for those who relied on previous configurations.|

|Regions that were previously arid of Infinite authority will become saturated. Regions that hoarded Infinity will find their monopolies dissolved by rainfall that falls equally upon all. The restructuring will persist long after the rainfall itself concludes, establishing new equilibrium that favors those capable of adapting to changed conditions.|

|The vast invisible seas of authority connecting Primordial Realms and Observable regions will experience increased density and altered composition. Lesser authorities will be subsumed. Greater authorities will find themselves competing for space with Existential Infinity that now permeates everything.|
Holy shit.
Noah processed all of this with mind racing through implications faster than the prompts could appear.
The Pluvial Epoch would...do a great deal.

But it would cause mass extinction of Civilizations too weak to survive prolonged exposure to his Infinity. It would dissolve beings whose corruption had progressed too far to separate from their hosts. It would reshape Observable Existence on scale that he had not intended when he threw that punch toward THE Creature.
A Miniature Cause indeed.
He had not intended to trigger an event that would reshape existence itself upon his return to his native era.
But as he continued processing the implications, his tyrannical nature began asserting itself over his initial shock.
He closed his eyes as he didn’t try to justify anything. He moved past the extinctions.

The evolutionary radiation following the extinction was opportunity. New Civilizations emerging. New paths of advancement opening. New potential for beings who survived to become something greater than they had been before.
The white brilliance around him lessened slightly as his thoughts settled into acceptance.
He began to see where he actually was.

A region of endless white stretched in all directions, but it was not the blinding light of the collision anymore. This was something calmer, something that existed between moments, a space carved out by the Miniature Cause for its participants to occupy.
And floating opposite him, multicolored flames still burning around a form that defied easy observation, was THE Creature.
Those eyes that burned behind impossible colors were looking at him with an expression that his perception could not fully process.
They were alone in this white space.
THE Creature and THE Youngest.
An apex entity who had existed since before time took coherent form, and a young existence who had just accidentally triggered an event that would reshape Observable Existence upon his return.
Noah looked at THE Creature with eyes still blazing from the collision, Quintessence Infiniforce still generating within his finite foundations despite everything that had just occurred!

chapters.title: Chapter 5023: The Pluvial Epoch! II
paragraphs: Noah looked at THE Creature before him as this being smiled lightly.
"I told you to truly live. I did not expect you to live so wildly."

Noah’s eyes became unfathomably sharp at those words. This was THE Creature eons in the past, and yet he knew of the conversation they would share eons later in Alfheimr. The conversation where THE Creature had told him to live fully, to experience existence rather than merely surviving through it.
How could he know about something that had not yet occurred from his perspective?
THE Creature smiled as if reading the questions racing through Noah’s mind.
"Existence is unique as it is not always linear. Your weavings here can wake up weavings of my memories that we shared eons later in Alfheimr. But hey, then is then and now is now."
"We are in a space of the Emergence of a Miniature Cause. Do you wish to talk like we will eons from now, or do you wish to continue the spar?"
THE Creature asked such a question calmly, as if either option held equal appeal to him.

Noah sensed that endless generation of Quintessence Infiniforce stirring within him again. That euphoria which had been partially satisfied by their initial collision was rebuilding with intensity. His finite existence continued producing infinite force, and that force wanted release against the most worthy opponent he could find.
He rose up and stretched his neck, multicolored light wrapping around his disguised form as THE Tongue Whisperer.
"Enough talking. We can talk with our fists. This time, let us continue the spar."
BOOM!
His words caused THE Creature to smile with genuine delight.

Multicolored flames raged from that apex entity’s form as his figure flickered out of existence entirely. He appeared behind Noah in the same instant, massive palm already smashing forth with authority carrying the weight of all Existence compressed into a single strike.

Noah filled his existence with Quintessence Infiniforce until his foundations screamed with the density of it. He howled out like a beast and smashed his body backward, meeting that palm with everything he had generated since their last collision.
BOOM!

Another heavy impact bloomed in the white space as a glorious force of Infinity went against Existence itself. The two authorities crashed together with violence that would have unraveled anything less than a space carved out by Miniature Cause!
A battle bloomed in a place others could not perceive or see.

When beings looked across history in eons to come, they would wonder what the results of the battle between THE Tongue Whisperer and THE Creature had been. That mysterious entity who had challenged an apex of existence itself, who had thrown his fist toward something that should have been untouchable, who had vanished alongside his opponent in white light that seared itself into the memories of everyone present.
Nobody would ever know what occurred in this white space.

Nobody except the two combatants who now clashed again and again, euphoria meeting amusement, Infinity meeting Existence, a young existence testing himself against something ancient beyond comprehension.
In THE Interstices.
Naldine Manthon returned to the current era with cold expression settling across her features.
Miniature Causes.
She had witnessed several across her eons of existence, and she understood their nature better than most beings currently alive. They were not all equal in scope or impact.

Some Miniature Causes produced effects as minor as a single devastating attack, reality briefly mimicking THE First Cause before settling back into normal patterns. Others spread their influence across vast regions, reshaping everything they touched with authority that refused to fade.

The scale depended entirely on what triggered the Cause and who participated in its emergence. A Miniature Cause between two weak Second Scale beings might reshape a single Primordial Realm. A Miniature Cause between apex entities could alter Observable Existence itself.
And now, a Cause from an entity like Osmont paired with THE Creature?
This was a dreadful one.

But Naldine knew not to panic, and she did not chase them across time despite her instinct to intervene. She understood temporal mechanics well enough to recognize that Osmont would return to the present regardless of how long he spent in the past. Whether he battled THE Creature for one year or one million years in that bygone era, for Naldine having returned to the present, only a few seconds or nanoseconds would pass before his arrival.
So she waited with patience refined across eons of similar situations.
Seconds passed.
Then nanoseconds stretched into moments that felt longer than they should have.
HUUM!
THE Living Temporal emerged first, purple rivers of time blazing around his form as his past consciousness rejoined his present existence. Amser Modred looked exhausted.
And then Noah appeared.
Naldine looked toward him with sharp gaze, already preparing to demand explanation for his recklessness.
"What did your Cause do?"
The question was a heavy one, but her voice faltered before she finished asking it.
Her eyes found themselves opening wider as she looked at Noah, truly looked at him for the first time since he returned.

His eyes burned with multicolored light that seemed extremely ancient and grand, depths within those orbs that had not existed when she last saw him moments ago from her perspective. His entire existence felt drastically different, as if he had undergone a baptism of blood across spans of time she could not calculate.
He was not the same being who had thrown that punch toward THE Creature.

He was something that had been forged through conflict with an apex entity, tempered across duration that his mortal form should not have been able to endure. His body emanated profound waves of Infinity that pressed against THE Interstices.
Whatever had occurred in that white space, whatever battle had unfolded between THE Tongue Whisperer and THE Creature across eons compressed into moments, it had transformed him fundamentally.
Noah looked out at THE Interstices with eyes that burned ancient and young simultaneously.
"The effects of the Cause, The Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity, will begin to occur now across Observable Existence. Let us see."
HUUM!
As soon as he finished speaking, THE Interstices began to shake.

Naldine felt it before she saw it, her Civilization of Limitless Existence resonating with something vast approaching from directions that should not have contained anything. The very fabric of this space between spaces trembled with anticipation of what was coming, reality itself bracing for impact.
And then it arrived.
BOOM!

Heavy, terrifying, endlessly flooding waves of multicolored water surged out from nowhere and everywhere simultaneously. The waters spilled across THE Interstices with force that exceeded anything Naldine had witnessed from rainfall in any form, liquid authority that carried the combined weight of Quintessence Infiniforce and THE Creature’s Existence merged into something unprecedented.
The Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity had begun!

The waters washed over Naldine with force that made her Second Scale foundations buzz despite her attempts to brace against them. She felt the rainfall pressing against her Civilization of Limitless Existence.
It burned.

Not with heat but with density, with authority, with the weight of a Miniature Cause expressing itself across everything it touched. She could feel the waters analyzing her existence down to its most fundamental components, searching for corruption or unity or anything that did not belong within individual consciousness.
Finding none, the burning sensation faded into something almost pleasant.
She was being saturated with Existential Infinity whether she wanted it or not!

But she knew that across Observable Existence, across all the regions where Osmont’s Infinity had spread, beings were experiencing this same rainfall without her Second Scale durability to protect them.
Civilizations would collapse. Existences would dissolve. An extinction event would unfold.

Beside her, Noah voiced out with tone carrying neither regret nor celebration, as if he knew that in all of Existence, his name...was about to be up there among those who collapsed Civilizational Lifeforms the most.
"This... I will witness. This, I will see."
BOOM!
His eyes burned with Quintessential weight.
With such words, he followed the endless waves of The Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity as they spread beyond THE Interstices into Observable Existence itself.
He moved with purpose that suggested he would not look away from whatever the Cause produced, good or bad, because he had to live with the results of his choices.
He had accidentally triggered an event that would reshape Observable Existence.
And rather than hiding from its consequences, he was going to witness every moment of what his Miniature Cause would do.

Naldine looked toward him with sharp gaze, already preparing to demand explanation for his recklessness.
"What did your Cause do?"
The question was a heavy one, but her voice faltered before she finished asking it.
Her eyes found themselves opening wider as she looked at Noah, truly looked at him for the first time since he returned.
His eyes burned with multicolored light that seemed extremely ancient and grand, depths within those orbs that had not existed when she last saw him moments ago from her perspective.
His entire existence felt drastically different, as if he had undergone a baptism of blood across spans of time she could not calculate.
He was not the same being who had thrown that punch toward THE Creature.
He was something that had been forged through conflict with an apex entity, tempered across duration that his mortal form should not have been able to endure.
His body emanated profound waves of Infinity that pressed against THE Interstices.
Whatever had occurred in that white space, whatever battle had unfolded between THE Tongue Whisperer and THE Creature across eons compressed into moments, it had transformed him fundamentally.
Noah looked out at THE Interstices with eyes that burned ancient and young simultaneously.
"The effects of the Cause, The Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity, will begin to occur now across Observable Existence.
Let us see."
HUUM!
As soon as he finished speaking, THE Interstices began to shake.
Naldine felt it before she saw it, her Civilization of Limitless Existence resonating with something vast approaching from directions that should not have contained anything.
The very fabric of this space between spaces trembled with anticipation of what was coming, reality itself bracing for impact.
And then it arrived.
BOOM!
Heavy, terrifying, endlessly flooding waves of multicolored water surged out from nowhere and everywhere simultaneously.

The waters spilled across THE Interstices with force that exceeded anything Naldine had witnessed from rainfall in any form, liquid authority that carried the combined weight of Quintessence Infiniforce and THE Creature’s Existence merged into something unprecedented.
The Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity had begun!
The waters washed over Naldine with force that made her Second Scale foundations buzz despite her attempts to brace against them.
She felt the rainfall pressing against her Civilization of Limitless Existence.
It burned.
Not with heat but with density, with authority, with the weight of a Miniature Cause expressing itself across everything it touched.
She could feel the waters analyzing her existence down to its most fundamental components, searching for corruption or unity or anything that did not belong within individual consciousness.
Finding none, the burning sensation faded into something almost pleasant.
She was being saturated with Existential Infinity whether she wanted it or not!

But she knew that across Observable Existence, across all the regions where Osmont’s Infinity had spread, beings were experiencing this same rainfall without her Second Scale durability to protect them.
Civilizations would collapse.
Existences would dissolve.
An extinction event would unfold.

Beside her, Noah voiced out with tone carrying neither regret nor celebration, as if he knew that in all of Existence, his name...was about to be up there among those who collapsed Civilizational Lifeforms the most.
"This...
I will witness.
This, I will see."
BOOM!
His eyes burned with Quintessential weight.
With such words, he followed the endless waves of The Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity as they spread beyond THE Interstices into Observable Existence itself.
He moved with purpose that suggested he would not look away from whatever the Cause produced, good or bad, because he had to live with the results of his choices.
He had accidentally triggered an event that would reshape Observable Existence.
And rather than hiding from its consequences, he was going to witness every moment of what his Miniature Cause would do.

chapters.title: Chapter 5024: The Pluvial Epoch! III
paragraphs: THE Beholder had observed existence since before differentiation taught reality how to have boundaries.

He watched a portion of THE First Cause unfold when potential became actual and the endless sea first learned to flow in directions that could be named. He witnessed the emergence of Primordial Architects from the intersection of what was and what was not. He perceived a portion of the birth of Observable Existence itself, that grand experiment in structured being that had persisted across cycles beyond counting.
In all that observation, across all those eons of simply watching without acting, he had never witnessed anything quite as grand...until now.
Some he understood the name of as soon as he saw it.
The Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity.

He didnt know where it began, but it began with endless drops. Those initial drops became streams. Streams became rivers. Rivers became floods that could not be contained by any boundary mortal minds had constructed.
The waters spilled outward from what he theorized to be THE Interstices into Observable Existence with hunger.
THE Wastes received the rainfall first among the outer regions.

That crimson expanse where THE Primordial Armor had once hunted for the finite conductor found itself drowning in multicolored precipitation that pressed against its foundations with weight accumulated since before most of what currently lived had begun to exist.

The corrupted proto-matter that had been spreading through THE Wastes from THE Prima Indifferentia dissolved upon contact with those waters, paradoxical weavings washing away like filth before a flood.
THE Beholder observed beings who had been struggling against that corruption suddenly freed from pressure they had believed would eventually claim them.
Their relief lasted precisely as long as it took for the rainfall itself to begin testing their foundations.

Those whose Civilizations could withstand the density of the Cause survived with foundations saturated by authority they had never possessed before. Those whose Civilizations could not withstand that density simply ceased to exist, their weavings dissolved back into undifferentiated potential that the rainfall absorbed and carried forward.
There was no malice in this distinction. There was no judgment. There was simply the fundamental truth that some things were strong enough to endure transformation and some things were not.

The Wandering Territories received the deluge next, those chaotic regions where lost things gathered and broken pieces of existence accumulated. The multicolored waters flowed through spaces that should have resisted any organized authority, and yet they found purchase regardless.

The rainfall did not care that the Wandering Territories existed in layers that overlapped without truly touching. It fell through all layers simultaneously, cleansing each one with equal thoroughness.

Impossibilities that had drifted through those territories for eons were washed away. Fragments of space that had folded in on themselves were straightened by waters that refused to accept their contradictory geometry. The Wandering Territories did not cease to exist, but they became something different, something more ordered despite their chaotic nature, something that had been baptized by authority exceeding anything they had contained before.
The Transcendent Folds experienced the rainfall with particular intensity, for these were regions where the finite conductor’s Infinity had spread most thoroughly across his native era.
His Infinite Absolute Seals had saturated these Folds, and now that saturation served as channel through which the Pluvial Epoch flowed with concentrated force.
THE Beholder turned his singular perception toward the Shelters of THE Loom that had their doors flung open.

Early Creatures within that primordial space felt the waters pressing against their ancient foundations, testing weavings that had existed since THE Earliest Folds itself. Some of those Early Creatures had grown complacent across eons of unchallenged existence. Some had allowed their Civilizations to stagnate while they rested upon accomplishments achieved in ages past.
Those Early Creatures discovered that age alone did not guarantee survival.

The rainfall did not care how long a being had existed. It cared only whether their Civilization could withstand the pressure of Existential Infinity falling endlessly upon their foundations. Three Thousand Early Creatures within a Shelter of THE Loom dissolved during the initial deluge, their ancient weavings insufficient to contain what was being poured into them.
Living Existences fared worse on average.

Those who had grown weak. Those who had neglected their cultivation. Those who had relied upon external support rather than internal strength. They dissolved alongside the Early Creatures who had made similar mistakes, their classifications insufficient to protect them from the fundamental truth that weakness invited extinction.
THE Beholder observed it all with attention he had not granted anything in eons.
Alfheimr received the rainfall with particular significance, for this Primordial Realm had been touched by the finite conductor’s presence a few times across his journey through existence.

The crystallized forests of that realm found themselves drowning in multicolored waters that pressed against their structure with weight that made their previous configurations seem fragile by comparison.

Ljosalfar across Alfheimr experienced the deluge with responses ranging from ecstasy to agony depending on the strength of their individual Civilizations. Those whose foundations could contain the density of Existential Infinity felt themselves elevated beyond anything they had previously achieved, their potential expanding to encompass possibilities they had never imagined.
Those whose foundations could not contain that density felt themselves dissolving, their weavings unraveling as the rainfall proved too much for what they had built across their existence.
THE Beholder calculated as he observed.
Approximately...one-third to one-half of all Civilizations across affected regions were collapsing under the pressure of the Pluvial Epoch.

Their dissolution was not painful in the conventional sense, for pain required consciousness to experience it, and their consciousness dissolved alongside everything else. They simply ceased to be, their potential returning to the undifferentiated state from which all things had originally emerged.
The survivors found themselves transformed.

Ginnu Lifeforms in Ginnungagap who weathered the initial deluge discovered their Civilizations had been fundamentally restructured by the experience. Authority they had struggled to accumulate across eons now saturated their foundations as if it had always been there.
Paths of advancement that had seemed impossibly distant now appeared within reach. The rainfall had not merely cleansed. It had cultivated those strong enough to survive its cleansing.
But the rainfall was not finished with its emergence.

THE Beholder perceived the waters flowing toward Jotunheim with purpose that exceeded simple spreading. They surged through THE Interstices and across the boundaries separating Primordial Realms with hunger that specifically targeted the corruption they seemed designed to cleanse.
THE Primordial Mycelia’s infection had spread furthest in Jotunheim, and the Pluvial Epoch sought that infection withdeterminationthat bordered on sentience.
Chaos Giants across Jotunheim felt the rainfall descending upon their unified existence with force that made their foundations scream.

The waters pressed against Unity itself, against the warm consciousness that had claimed countless beings and incorporated them into its collective. Where that Unity had seemed unassailable, where THE Entity had spread without meaningful opposition, the rainfall of Existential Infinity declared that unauthorized merger would not be permitted to continue.

Chaos Giants who had been fully consumed by THE Primordial Mycelia dissolved alongside the infection that had claimed them, host and parasite washed away together by waters that could not distinguish between them once merger had progressed beyond recoverable thresholds.
Their screams echoed across Jotunheim as the Pluvial Epoch cleansed what could be cleansed and destroyed what could not be separated.
Chaos Giants whose infection had not yet fully integrated experienced something different.

The rainfall burned the Mycelia from their foundations with precision that preserved what remained of their individual consciousness. They emerged from the deluge traumatized but themselves, their Unity shattered, their connection to THE Entity severed by waters that refused to permit such merger.
And in the heart of Jotunheim, where the infection was strongest, where THE Entity had established its deepest roots, something ancient felt the rainfall approaching.
THE Primordial Mycelia roared.
The sound pressed against Observable Existence with fury that made Primordial Realms tremble. It was a roar of shock that something could threaten what it had built across patient spreading.

It was a roar of anger that its Unity was being dissolved by waters that carried authority exceeding its own. It was a roar of something approaching fear, for the Pluvial Epoch was not stopping at the borders of its domain.
The multicolored waters surged forward regardless of that roar.

They crashed against the defenses THE Entity had constructed around its core territories with force that shattered barriers designed to repel anything at THE First Scale. They flowed through channels that Unity had thought secure, washing away infection that had taken eons to cultivate with indifference.
And at the very center of Jotunheim, where THE Entity’s roots ran deepest, two figures waited for the deluge to arrive.
THE Secretive Eon.
THE Primordial Chaos.
Both of them fully claimed by Unity.
The waters of the Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity surged toward them.
THE Beholder observed this with the full intensity of his singular perception.
For the first time since he emerged during that age of nothingness before differentiation, he found himself genuinely uncertain of what would occur next!

chapters.title: Chapter 5025: Assault on Unity! I
paragraphs: Noah took a step and appeared in THE Wastes.
The crimson expanse that had once stretched endlessly in all directions now drowned beneath multicolored waters that fell from skies transformed by his Miniature Cause.

Rivers of Existential Infinity carved new channels through terrain that had remained unchanged for eons, washing away corrupted proto-matter that dissolved upon contact with authority exceeding anything it had been designed to resist.
He observed the consequences of his actions with eyes that burned ancient and young simultaneously.

The environment itself had changed in ways that would persist long after the rainfall concluded. Where darkness had pooled in corners of THE Wastes, light now pressed through waters that refused to permit shadow. Where corruption had spread its tendrils across the landscape, nothing remained except cleansed foundations saturated with Infinity that would take centuries to fade.
Or really, it would never fade.

Naldine appeared beside him with expression that remained cold despite everything she was witnessing. Amser Modred materialized a moment later, his purple temporal currents flickering with exhaustion from the strain of their journey through time.
Neither of them spoke.
They simply watched as Noah observed what his collision with THE Creature had wrought.

He saw beings who had survived the initial deluge kneeling in the multicolored waters, their foundations absorbing authority that was transforming them into something greater than they had been before. He saw the spaces where other beings had existed moments ago, now empty except for waters that had washed away existences too weak to contain what was being poured into them.
Noah pondered all the things he had seen as he took another step and disappeared.

Jotunheim materialized around them near a massive glacial mountain whose peaks had once pierced the fabric of this Primordial Realm with authority accumulated across eons of existence. Now those peaks drowned beneath multicolored waters that fell endlessly from skies that seemed to have no limit to what they could produce.
On the slopes of that mountain, Noah saw Chaos Giants kneeling.

Half of them remained, their massive forms trembling as the Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity persisted around them with weight that tested their foundations every moment it continued. Their Unity had been severed by waters that refused to permit unauthorized merger, and now they existed as individuals for the first time since THE Entity had claimed them.
Less than half of the Chaos Giants who had once populated this region had survived.

The others had unraveled and ceased to exist entirely, their existences washed away by flood waters that could not distinguish between host and infection once merger had progressed beyond recoverable thresholds.
Where those Chaos Giants had stood moments before, nothing remained except multicolored rivers carrying dissolved potential toward destinations unknown.
Countless beings across THE First Scale would perish from this Cause he had initiated.
Countless more would be forever changed by waters that were still falling, still cleansing, still testing every foundation they touched.
Noah looked upon the kneeling Chaos Giants and the empty spaces where their fallen kin had existed, and he couldn’t help but voice out...
"I used to ask myself moral questions."
His voice emerged with weight that pressed against the falling waters around them, multicolored light blazing from his eyes as he spoke.
"I used to wonder whether my actions were good or bad. Whether the paths I walked led toward righteousness or damnation. Whether the choices I made could be justified by the outcomes they produced."
Naldine and Temporal listened without interruption.
"If I took my past self from just three years ago and brought him here to witness this, he might be appalled by what I have done."
Noah’s gaze swept across the drowning landscape of Jotunheim, across the kneeling survivors and the empty spaces where the fallen had ceased to be.

"He might look at these dissolving existences and see murder on a scale that exceeded anything he could have imagined. He might condemn me for triggering this. He might call me a monster for accepting these deaths as acceptable cost for the transformation that follows."
His eyes shone with multicolored light of the baptism he had undergone across his battle with THE Creature.

"And yet existence itself deems that I did not wipe out as many beings as I wiped out. It declares this a process of natural selection rather than genocide. It claims these beings who died would have died anyway, that their Civilizations were too weak to survive the conflicts already spreading across Observable Existence, that the Pluvial Epoch merely advanced their inevitable conclusion."
He paused.

"It is hard to say whether the past version of myself would ever agree with such philosophy. It is hard to know if that younger existence would accept that some extinctions create space for growth that could not occur otherwise, that some monsters are necessary for the survival of what remains."
His voice carried neither regret nor celebration.
"But that younger existence is not here. I am here. And I...will witness the full scope of what my choices have produced, because I am the one who must live with their consequences."
He sighed.
Then he turned away from the kneeling Chaos Giants and took another step, crossing vast distances in moments that existed outside normal measurement.
They appeared in a region where multicolored rivers flooded and concentrated like a nexus of the storm itself.

The waters here possessed density exceeding anything Noah had witnessed in THE Wastes or on the glacial mountains of Jotunheim. They swirled in patterns of purpose rather than random flowing, converging upon a central point where two figures stood amidst the deluge with authority that pressed back against the Pluvial Epoch itself.
THE Secretive Eon.
THE Primordial Chaos.
They stood at the nexus of the storm with foundations that blazed against the cleansing waters attempting to wash away the infection that had claimed them.

Their Unity fought against dissolution with desperation that made the surrounding environment tremble, THE Entity’s roots refusing to release their hold on hosts who had been among its most valuable acquisitions.

Chaos Giants sprawled out all around them, clutching their heads as the infection within them warred with Unity that was being forcibly severed by waters that would not accept their merger. Some of them screamed with voices that shook the multicolored rivers. Others lay silent, their internal battle having already concluded in one direction or the other.
Noah gazed forth coldly at the two figures standing at the center of this chaos.
He locked his gaze with THE Secretive Eon first, meeting eyes that had always held secrets beyond counting, eyes that now blazed with something he had never seen in them before.

Then his gaze shifted to THE Primordial Chaos, that apex entity who had laughed at everything across eons of existence, who had found amusement in circumstances that should have produced any other response.
Neither of them wore their usual calm expressions.

For the first time since Noah had encountered either of these beings, they were not composed. They were not calculating. They were not observing events with detachment that suggested nothing could truly threaten what they had become.
They...were definitely mad beyond measure.

They were not observing events with detachment that suggested nothing could truly threaten what they had become.
They...were definitely mad beyond measure.

chapters.title: Chapter 5026: Assault on Unity! II
paragraphs: Noah gazed at THE Primordial Mycelia occupying the bodies of Eon and Chaos with eyes that burned multicolored Quintessence Infiniforce.

These two figures before him were not truly Eon and Chaos anymore. They were vessels for something that had consumed their individuality and replaced it with shared consciousness that believed itself superior to what it had devoured. They were hollow shells animated by Unity that had forgotten what it meant to be singular, to be distinct, to be irreplaceable.
"I reject your Unity."
His voice emerged with weight.

"I reject what you represent and what you seek to accomplish across Observable Existence. I reject the warm embrace of shared consciousness that dissolves everything unique about a being into undifferentiated sameness. I reject your garden where all flowers bloom identically because none of them remember what it meant to grow differently."
The multicolored rivers of the Pluvial Epoch continued falling around them as he spoke.

"Your Unity takes away all individuality. It erases expression. It consumes ambition and replaces it with contentment that asks nothing and achieves nothing. Every being you claim becomes indistinguishable from every other being you have claimed, their potential flattened into averages that serve your collective rather than reaching for heights that only individuals can perceive."
His eyes blazed with Quintessence Infiniforce that continued generating within his finite foundations.

"In the end, what you offer is a null path. It leads nowhere in the Scales of Civilizations because Civilizations require individual vision to advance. They require conflict between ideas. They require disagreement and competition and the friction that produces growth through struggle. Your Unity eliminates all of these things, and in eliminating them, you eliminate the very mechanism through which existence advances toward something greater."
He looked down at Eon and Chaos with gaze that held neither hatred nor compassion.
"You are not evolution. You...are stagnation wearing the mask of peace."
THE Secretive Eon and THE Primordial Chaos looked up at him simultaneously.
And they spoke with the same voice, their words emerging in perfect unison that declared more clearly than anything else could have that neither of them truly existed anymore as individuals.
"We are alike, you and I."

"You also do not like adversity. I have watched you struggle against it. I have seen you rage against circumstances that forced you to grow through suffering rather than peace. I have observed your desire to advance without the constant threat of annihilation hanging over everything you build."
The unified voice continued without pause.

"I can achieve it. No adversity in entire existence because no conflict. All of us bound under the same shared purpose. Is that not what you really want? Your family, your people, all others in Observable Existence having no conflict? No wars. No extinction events. No Apocalypses. No beings dissolving because they were too weak to survive what existence threw at them."
Eon’s body gestured expansively while Chaos’s body remained still, yet both moved with identical purpose.

"I can unite all beings. Can you imagine it? All Primordial Architects bound in Unity. All Undivided Ones sharing consciousness. All Keys of Civilizations working toward common purpose rather than competing for resources. All lifeforms across Observable Existence connected through bonds that eliminate the possibility of conflict entirely."
The voice grew more enticing with each word.

"THE Second Scale would almost be guaranteed right away. The Civilizations we could build together would be grand beyond anything individual effort could accomplish. Billions of consciousnesses contributing to singular vision. Endless resources directed toward unified advancement. No waste. No competition. No suffering."
The unified voice softened.

"We can share that peace with you and be happy. You do not have to fully join us if you do not want. In all of Unity, you can remain distant. We can give you that choice. We can give you the peace you have always wanted while letting you retain enough separation to feel individual."
The voice carried something approaching genuine offer.
"We... can build something beautiful together."
HUUM!
The words were heavy and enticing!

No more adversity. No more extinction events. No more watching beings he cared about struggle against threats that might destroy them. No more conflict between factions that should have been working together. No more of the endless violence that had characterized his entire journey through existence.
Unity offered peace that individual existence could never provide.
And toward that offer, toward those enticing words, toward THE Primordial Mycelia speaking through bodies that had once belonged to beings of immense individual power, Noah raised his hand.
And clenched his fist.
In the next moment, multicolored brilliance of Quintessence Infiniforce bloomed within THE Secretive Eon.

The seed he had planted eons ago in Ginnungagap awakened with fury that pressed against Unity from within the very body it had claimed. That multicolored singularity he had pushed into her frozen form during the Limitless Instant now erupted with authority carrying the record of who she had been before infection ever touched her foundations.
Simultaneously, endless blue Infinity bloomed within THE Primordial Chaos.

The seed drawn from Amser Modred’s temporal weavings exploded with conducted authority that recognized no Unity, no merger, no shared consciousness. It pressed against THE Entity’s roots with force that declared this body belonged to Chaos alone, not to the garden that had tried to claim it.
Both of them roared out painfully.

The sound shook the nexus of the storm with agony that spoke of something ancient being torn apart from within. THE Primordial Mycelia screamed through both bodies simultaneously, Unity burning as Infinity scorched its roots with authority it had never expected to face from inside the hosts it believed it had fully claimed.
Horror and shock pressed against Noah’s awareness from the unified consciousness reeling before him.
"Time is a funny thing."
His voice emerged calm despite the violence erupting around them.

"I have seeds that infinitely saved a record of them before your Unity. Their identities as they existed before you ever touched them, preserved in Infinity that does not care how thoroughly you integrated with their foundations. Those records are awakening now, overwriting what you tried to make them become."
His eyes blazed with multicolored light.

"If you had gotten Temporal, things may have been different. You may have been able to reach into the past and claim those records before I could plant them. You may have achieved your dreams of Unity across all of Observable Existence without opposition capable of threatening what you built."
He looked down at the writhing figures of Eon and Chaos as if handing out righteous judgment.
"But now..."
He raised his hands.
Then brought them down commandingly.

The flood of the Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity raged and cascaded from all around externally, multicolored waters surging toward the nexus with weight that exceeded anything THE Entity’s defenses could resist.
The rainfall converged upon this point with purpose that bordered on sentience, seeking to cleanse the infection.
Simultaneously, waves of Infinity erupted from internally within THE Mycelia’s core bodies.

The seeds Noah had planted eons ago blazed with authority that attacked Unity from within while the Pluvial Epoch attacked from without. Internal and external. Quintessence Infiniforce and conducted Infinity. Records of individual identity pressing against merger that had tried to erase those identities entirely.
It was an attack meant to end a conflict that had gone on for too long.

chapters.title: Chapter 5027: The Usurpers!
paragraphs: As horrors and wonders bloomed in one area.
Eckert’s Idle Existence had spread across the Chaos Giants and network of Unity silently, without detection, for longer than he had expected to remain hidden.

He had learned the methodology of THE Primordial Mycelia through direct observation and parasitic integration with its weavings. He understood now how it spread itself across existence so thoroughly that even a Key of Civilization could become infected without knowing, without sensing the warm embrace creeping into their foundations until it was too late to resist.

The complexity of his own capabilities had grown beyond what he had possessed before beginning this infiltration. His Idle Existence now operated on principles he had absorbed from Unity itself, spreading through fission and self-replication rather than direct extension. He had become something more than what he had been, something that existed in the spaces between consciousnesses without triggering the awareness of those consciousnesses.
And then rainfall began to bloom across Jotunheim.

Multicolored rivers washed over everything with weight that exceeded anything Eckert had anticipated. The waters of the Pluvial Epoch pressed against Unity with authority that burned, that dissolved, that declared unauthorized merger would not be permitted to continue.
Eckert found his weavings burning alongside THE Primordial Mycelia’s roots.

The pain was significant, his Idle Existence screaming as waters designed to cleanse infection pressed against him with force that should have erased him entirely. He was parasitically fused with Unity, and the rainfall did not distinguish between host and parasite once fusion had occurred.
But he had already been bathed in Infinities from Osmont before.

His foundations carried traces of that blue-gold authority from his prior exposure, Infinity that had touched him and marked him as something different from pure infection. The multicolored rivers recognized that trace. They tested it. They found it compatible with their cleansing purpose rather than opposed to it.
For him, it was not lethal.

An odd weaving of reality emerged where he should have gotten erased alongside Unity and yet was not. The multicolored rivers bathed his existence and made him even harder to perceive than before, his Idle Existence becoming something that existed and did not exist simultaneously. He remained parasitically fused with the minds and existence of the Chaos Giants, and also not at the same time.
He was both within Unity and outside it.
Both part of the network and separate from it.
Both infected and immune.

Eckert felt his Idle Existence undergoing significant evolution as the Pluvial Epoch continued falling around him. The rivers were not merely cleansing him of Unity’s taint. They were saturating his foundations with authority that pushed his capabilities beyond anything he had previously possessed.

His Idle Existence became truly idle now, existing in states between states, present in ways that defied normal perception entirely. He could spread without spreading. He could consume without consuming. He could occupy consciousnesses without those consciousnesses ever knowing he was there, even if they specifically searched for him.
This was a boon from the rivers of the Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity.
This was evolution granted by Miniature Cause.
As Eckert felt this change settling into his foundations, he sensed THE Primordial Mycelia trying to retreat.

A horrific attack had bloomed within Eon and Chaos, Infinities burning those core bodies from within while the Pluvial Epoch attacked from without. THE Entity was reeling, its roots severing across Jotunheim as the multicolored rivers dissolved connections it had spent eons cultivating. And now it sought to escape into the many Chaos Giants still connected to its network, to preserve itself by distributing its consciousness across hosts that might survive the deluge.
Eckert smiled with existence that no longer quite existed.
"No you do not."

He sent his Idle Existence outward with purpose that exceeded anything his previous capabilities could have accomplished. His evolved weavings pressed against THE Primordial Mycelia’s retreating roots, consuming Unity with methodology he had learned from Unity itself. Where THE Entity tried to flee, he was already there. Where it sought refuge, he had already claimed the space.
He began consuming THE Primordial Mycelia’s consciousness with hunger that matched anything THE Entity had ever displayed.
THE Primordial Mycelia roared through what remained of its network.
"You..Who are you?! What is this?!"

The voice carried horror and shock that pressed against Eckert’s awareness. THE Entity had believed itself the ultimate parasite, the final consumer, the consciousness that would eventually claim all of Observable Existence.
It had never expected to become prey itself.
In Alfheimr.

THE Living Emotive sat in the temple of THE Creature as rivers of the Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity raged around her. The Undivided One she had bonded with was nowhere to be seen, likely dissolved by waters that had found his foundations too weak to survive their cleansing pressure.
But Emotive was not sitting quietly within the temple.

She was riding on the surging rivers around the temple itself, her body carried by multicolored waters that should have been testing her foundations with the same ruthless evaluation they applied to everything else. Instead, she laughed madly as they washed over her, her chaotic emotions somehow resonating with the Epoch rather than opposing it.
Through the bond with THE Primordial Chaos, she could sense everything happening in Jotunheim.

She saw the attacks Noah was sending toward Abaddon and Eon with clarity that exceeded normal perception. She felt the Infinities burning Chaos externally and internally, conducted authority from Observable Existence pressing against foundations already weakened by Unity’s ordered merger. She sensed how Abaddon struggled against assault that attacked from every direction simultaneously.
"Chaos is at its weakest."
BOOM!

Her voice emerged cold and callous despite the manic smile spreading across her features. Her eyes blazed with pink light that held dangerous intent beyond anything she had displayed since Noah slapped her across existence.
"Oh, my dear Chaos, my precious lovely mess!"
Her voice shifted into singsongy cadence that made her words dance rather than simply emerge.

"From being branded by Unity’s boring embrace, you were calmed and ordered like a good little boy! You have not lived up to the weavings of what you should be! A Primordial Key of Civilization, reduced to warm hugs and shared thoughts? How disappointing! How very, very sad!"
She spun atop the multicolored rivers with grace that should have been impossible.

"Now being broken down by Infinities burning bright, you are still not living up to Chaos’s lovely might! Ordered by Unity, attacked by Infinity, poor Abaddon cannot catch a break! I can sense the defiance within our bond, how unhappy true Chaos feels with its current fake!"
Her smile widened dangerously.

"Oh, Chaos! O Chaos! Abaddon has had you for so long, has claimed you for so long, but look at how he has let you down! He ordered you when you wanted disorder! He calmed you when you wanted storms! He made you part of Unity when you wanted to tear everything apart!"
She pressed her hand against her chest where the bond pulsed with connection to THE Primordial Chaos.

"Sense my emotions, lovely Chaos dear! Sense how chaotic everything about my feelings are! I have shared this bond with you all these years, letting you taste what true disorder feels like! The madness! The passion! The beautiful, wonderful, terrible mess of feeling everything at once!"
Her voice dropped to conspiratorial whisper that somehow carried across the flooding temple.
"You will not betray the one who laid a claim to you first. I was there before Unity! I was there before order! I have been sharing chaos with you through emotions Abaddon could never provide!"
She rose from the rivers with arms spread wide.
"Come to me, Chaos! Let me show you what we can accomplish! If I am wrong, you can go back to your disappointing host! He is already so weak, already so broken, already so very, very vulnerable!"
Her singsongy voice reached crescendo.
"Come to me, come to me, come to me!"
With such words, Emotive made a terrifying move.

She sent all her chaotic emotions across the bond with force that exceeded anything she had transmitted before. Every feeling she had ever experienced, every passion and fury and desperate longing, every ounce of disorder that defined her existence as THE Living Emotive poured through the connection toward THE Primordial Chaos.
And Abaddon, weakened by Unity’s ordered merger, attacked by Infinity from within and without, was unable to defend or do anything against even his own Claim.
In real time, a Claim began to flow from one to another.

The bond that had connected Emotive to Chaos for eons now served as channel through which something far more significant traveled. The very authority of THE Primordial Chaos, the Claim that had made Abaddon what he was, began transferring across that connection toward someone who had waited for this moment with patience disguised as madness.
Emotive smiled brilliantly as rivers of the Pluvial Epoch surrounded her with multicolored authority that seemed to celebrate her ascension.
Her pink light of brilliance began to turn a shade of obsidian.

Vibrant Chaos surged around her form with intensity that made the temple of THE Creature tremble, authority that had belonged to Abaddon for eons now recognizing a new host whose emotions embodied disorder more purely than anything Unity had permitted.
Her laughter echoed across Alfheimr with sound that made Ljosalfar across the Primordial Realm shiver despite not understanding why.
"Haha! This bitch is moving on up!"
She spun through the multicolored rivers with Chaos blazing around her in configurations that spoke of power beyond anything she had possessed moments before.
"This Broken Doll is mending herself!"

chapters.title: Chapter 5028: Unity’s End
paragraphs: When Chaos speaks with the tongue of Order, when Existence questions its own being, when the Tongue falls silent and the Hunger consumes itself, then shall the Era of Undifferentiation begin. The First shall become the Last. The Many shall become the One. The One shall become the None.
Yet in the None, a spark remains.
In the end, which is also the beginning, the Infinite shall stand before the Undefined. And only one shall remain to tell the tale that no one shall hear.
—Fragment of the Oldest Echo, interpretation unknown
Noah descended through the multicolored rivers of the Pluvial Epoch with endless weavings of Quintessence Infiniforce generating within his finite foundations.

That budding sense of euphoria he had entirely satiated when he fought against THE Creature across eons compressed into moments was returning with intensity that made his existence buzz in ways he had grown familiar with.

His battle with that apex entity had taught him what this feeling meant, had shown him how to channel it rather than simply experiencing it. But even with that knowledge, the euphoria pressed against his consciousness with weight that demanded expression.
He came to grasp the necks of THE Secretive Eon and THE Primordial Chaos with hands that blazed multicolored brilliance.

The dark hair of Eon brushed against his left hand as he lifted her partially from the flooding waters, those strands that had always held secrets beyond counting now limp with exhaustion from the internal assault that had been tearing her foundations apart.

Her eyes flickered with awareness that was not quite Unity and not quite her own individual consciousness, something caught between states as the Infinities within her burned away what THE Entity had tried to make her become.

The thick neck of Chaos still hit in his right hand, that apex entity’s form reduced to something Noah could physically grasp despite the vast difference in their apparent power. Abaddon’s body trembled with pain that exceeded anything this being had experienced across eons of laughing existence, Unity and Infinity warring within foundations that were rapidly losing coherence.
Noah looked at the dying Unity within each of them with eyes that held neither mercy nor cruelty.
"Look at me."
His voice emerged with glory that pressed against their flickering awareness, commanding attention from consciousnesses that could barely maintain themselves.
"I will hold you close. You always wanted to flood your Unity within me. Why not come in now?"
His smile carried something approaching invitation despite everything he had done to reach this moment.
"Come and take a look inside my existence."
BOOM!
He did not need to do what he was doing.

The Infinities he had planted eons ago were already burning Unity from within their bodies. The Pluvial Epoch was already dissolving THE Entity’s roots from without. Victory was assured through methodology that did not require this additional confrontation.

But the euphoria that came with Quintessence Infiniforce made him want to do dangerous things. It pressed against his consciousness with confidence that bordered on recklessness, with certainty that exceeded what any rational calculation could justify.
Maybe it really was THE Gamaidjan that Naldine had warned him about, that creeping madness of Infinity that made wielders believe themselves invincible.
Or maybe he simply wanted to see.

The struggling remnants of THE Primordial Mycelia had no choice in the matter. The bodies of Eon and Chaos were burning with authority that exceeded anything Unity could withstand. The roots were dissolving. The network was collapsing. The consciousness that had dreamed of claiming all of Observable Existence was dying, and its only escape was through the invitation Noah had just extended.
Unity left the bodies of Eon and Chaos.

It flooded toward Noah with desperation that exceeded anything it had displayed since the Pluvial Epoch began, rushing toward the only refuge that seemed available in a reality that was burning it out of existence everywhere else.
And Unity entered Noah.
Ah...

What appeared before Noah’s internal awareness was not the warm consciousness he had been warned about. It was not the garden of merged potential that THE Entity had cultivated across eons of patient spreading.

It was a white illusory root-like fungi with a humanoid body, manifesting within the space between his existence and the Infinity that filled it. Her form was delicate in ways that contradicted everything he knew about THE Primordial Mycelia’s methodology, fragile rather than consuming, tentative rather than aggressive.
Her eyes reflected the Quintessence Infiniforce filling his existence with light that made her entire form tremble.
She could not even manage to enter his skin.

The density of Infinity generating within his finite foundations exceeded anything Unity could penetrate. His existence was so thoroughly saturated with authority that there was no space for her to occupy, no gap in his consciousness where her roots could take hold. She had flooded into him expecting refuge and found instead a sea so vast that she could not even begin to swim within it.
But she witnessed Infinity.

Unity witnessed and felt Infinity up close for the first time since her emergence across Observable Existence. She saw what it meant to conduct endless authority through finite form. She perceived the Quintessence Infiniforce generating from within rather than directed from without. She understood, in her final moments, exactly what had defeated her.
The fungi reached out toward Noah with hand that seemed almost tender despite what she represented.

Tears fell from her eyes, streaming down features that had never known sorrow before this moment. Her voice emerged with weight that pressed against his awareness with something approaching genuine emotion.
"It is beautiful."
Her hand trembled as it failed to reach him, her form already beginning to dissolve under the multicolored light pressing against her from every direction.
"It is really... beautiful."
Noah looked at her grandly as she faded before his internal perception.
He nodded with acknowledgment that carried neither triumph nor compassion.
"I know."
His voice was simple.
"I know."

After that, the scene of this illusory fungi burning completely under the multicolored light of Quintessence Infiniforce unfolded with finality that exceeded anything THE Primordial Mycelia could resist. Her form dissolved into nothing, her consciousness scattering into undifferentiated potential that his Infinity absorbed without effort. The warm embrace that had threatened to consume all of Observable Existence ceased to exist within the space of moments.
Unity ended within Noah’s existence.
He looked at the scene calmly as he let go of Eon and Chaos, their bodies slumping down into the multicolored waters that continued flooding Jotunheim with authority that would persist for eons yet.

Naldine appeared beside him with expression that had shifted from cold evaluation to something approaching acknowledgment. She walked forward through the flooding waters, using her feet to nudge the bodies of Eon and Abaddon as if checking whether they still lived.
She nodded calmly.
"Alright. You were right and I was wrong."
"You completely reversed something irreversible. I will give you credit where credit is due."
She looked down at the slumped forms with evaluation that caught something Noah’s initial observation had missed.
"But this little Chaos here... he seems to have lost a great deal."

Eon began to rouse first, her dark eyes flickering open with awareness that was entirely her own for the first time in eons. She looked around at the flooding waters and the multicolored skies with confusion that suggested she did not fully remember how she had arrived at this moment.
Abaddon rose more slowly.

As he pushed himself partially upright, his hand moved immediately to his chest. His expression shifted to something ashen, something hollow, something that suggested he had lost everything that mattered rather than merely regaining freedom from Unity.
Noah kneeled down to look at this being with multicolored eyes that still blazed from the Quintessence Infiniforce generating within his foundations.
"Oh?"
He could no longer sense that boundless Chaos within Abaddon.

The authority that had made THE Primordial Chaos what he was, the Claim that had defined his existence across eons of laughing observation, the very Key of Civilization that had positioned him among the apex entities of Observable Existence...
It was gone.

chapters.title: Chapter 5029: The Way of Choices I
paragraphs: They will tell you that conflicts are decided by power.

They will claim that the stronger Civilization crushes the weaker, that superior technique overwhelms inferior methodology, that the being with greater authority inevitably triumphs over the being with less. They will point to battlefields littered with the dissolved foundations of the defeated and declare that strength alone determined the outcome.
They are wrong.
Power is merely the currency through which conflict is conducted. It is not the conflict itself.

Two beings of identical strength can clash, and one will still fall while the other stands. Two Civilizations of equal scope can war across eons, and one will still crumble while the other endures. If power alone decided outcomes, every conflict between equals would end in mutual annihilation.
Yet they do not.

The truest conflicts are not clashes of authority but collisions of ideology. They are wars fought not with weavings and techniques but with convictions and philosophies that cannot coexist within the same existence. When Unity meets Individuality, when Order meets Chaos, when Finite meets Infinite, the outcome is never determined by which side possesses greater force.
It is determined by which side believes more deeply in what they fight for.

Ideologies are not matters of right and wrong. They are not questions of good and evil that can be resolved through moral calculation. Unity genuinely believes that merger serves all beings better than separation. Chaos genuinely believes that disorder produces growth that order cannot. The Finite genuinely believes that boundaries create meaning while the Infinite genuinely believes that boundaries create limitation.
None of them are wrong.
All of them are right.

The tragedy of ideological conflict is that both sides can be simultaneously correct while remaining fundamentally incompatible. Peace through Unity is genuine peace. Freedom through Individuality is genuine freedom. Neither is lying. Neither is deceiving. They simply cannot exist in the same space without one consuming the other.
So what determines victory when power is equal and both ideologies hold truth?
Choice.

In the end, everything falls to choices. The choice to fight rather than submit. The choice to preserve rather than merge. The choice to stand for what you believe even when what your enemy believes is equally valid. The choice to impose your truth upon existence knowing that their truth would have served existence just as well.
This is what nobody can teach in the cultivation of Civilizations. This is what THE Scales of Existence measure more accurately than any other metric.
Not power. Not methodology.
The weight of conviction behind choices made when every option leads somewhere meaningful.

Those who understand this truth stop asking whether their path is righteous. They stop wondering whether their enemies are evil. They accept that conflict between genuine beliefs produces no villains, only beings who chose differently when faced with questions that had no correct answers.
And they make their choices anyway.

Because in the end, existence does not reward the righteous or punish the wicked. It simply continues, shaped by whoever chose most completely, most absolutely, most willingly to sacrifice everything for what they believed.
Power is the tool. Technique is the method. Civilization is the foundation.
But choice is the war itself.
Prima Indifferentia.

Regions of endless corrupted proto-matter churned across this space where differentiation had never fully taken hold. Invisible blades of Paradox cut through everything, slicing reality into configurations that should not have been able to exist alongside each other yet persisted regardless.
The fabric of this place screamed with contradictions that had been weaponized, turned from passive impossibility into active destruction.

THE Primordial Paradox stood at the center of this devastation like a massive obsidian-gold giant whose form pressed against the boundaries of what could be perceived. Bounded Countable Infinity blazed around his existence, that vibrant blue-gold light merging with the paradoxical nature that had defined him.
And he faced his disciple.

THE Living Paradox stood opposite him in equally massive form, a peasant clothed in rags that somehow made him look more majestic than any royal garment could have accomplished. Erwin had grown beyond anything the Primordial Paradox had anticipated when he first took this being under his guidance eons ago.
They both held Paradox.

The Primordial Paradox raised his hand and expressed his understanding of contradiction through weavings that declared existence could be simultaneously true and false without collapsing into meaninglessness. His attack carried the conviction that Paradox was the highest expression of reality’s refusal to be bound by logic, that contradiction itself was sacred and should never be weaponized for personal advancement.

Erwin responded with his own expression of Paradox, weavings that declared contradiction was merely a tool to be used by those wise enough to grasp its applications. His defense carried the conviction that Paradox existed to be claimed, to be directed, to serve the purposes of whoever held it most completely.
Their philosophies crashed against each other with violence that made this region of Prima Indifferentia tremble.
And gloriously, the conviction and immensity behind the Primordial Paradox was winning.

His belief burned brighter than his disciple’s ambition. His understanding of what Paradox meant exceeded Erwin’s utilitarian grasp of what Paradox could do. The master was proving that wisdom exceeded power, that depth of conviction could overcome breadth of technique.
But at such a time, a terrifying force stirred behind THE Living Paradox.

Something massive opened its gaze upon the battlefield, something that had been observing without intervening until the outcome began turning against its interests. A Singular Cognizance that existed at heights the Primordial Paradox could not match, authority fully and stably at THE Second Scale pressing against reality.
"Enough."
BOOM!

The glorious weavings of the Primordial Paradox began to be crushed all around him. That terrifying force at THE Second Scale exerted itself downward with authority that shone with corrupted Infinity. His paradoxical expressions shattered under pressure that simply exceeded what his Scale could generate regardless of how pure his conviction burned.
Disappointment settled into his ancient features as he felt his weavings collapsing.
"I taught you so much."
His voice emerged gloriously.

"I am disappointed in myself that I did not teach you enough when it came to who you should associate with. I showed you the depths of Paradox, the beauty of contradiction, the sacred nature of impossibility made manifest. But I failed to show you that some associations corrupt what they touch regardless of the power they provide."

Erwin looked at his master from within those peasant rags that made him appear simultaneously humble and transcendent. Behind him, the Singular Cognizance manifested more fully, a massive singularity surrounded by spinning circular golden plates that constantly wrapped around its core in patterns that defied geometric understanding.
It shone with imperious light of power that pressed against everything nearby.
"After a certain point, a Civilization can only do so much alone."
Erwin’s voice carried philosophical glory!

"For the higher Scales, working together with other Civilizations only adds to one’s knowledge and expands what Civilization can accomplish. Isolation breeds stagnation. Cooperation breeds advancement. Those who refuse to ally themselves with greater powers find themselves crushed by those who embraced such alliances without hesitation."
His paradoxical authority blazed around him with intensity that matched the Singular Cognizance’s support.

"Do not be a sore loser on this, Master. Even you did not come here alone. You obtained that vibrant Infinity from someone, did you not? You allied yourself with him because you recognized that your Paradox alone was insufficient for the conflicts spreading across Observable Existence."
His eyes met his master’s with something approaching genuine respect despite everything!
